#7 Cable tv.  No one complained when I put the Real Housewives on New Jersey on.

If you have to be at a laundromat, this is hands down the best one to be at.

Came to this location based on other popular Yelp reviews and was very satisfied. The location is very clean and reasonably priced. The staff seemed very friendly although I did not have to personally interact with them. One issue might be availability of machines during peak times. My visit was around 3:00pm on a Saturday and I had no issues. There is free WIFI too! Overall, very pleased and I will definitely visit again.

ok, so no one likes to do laundry and no one wants to pay for it. but i really have no complaints about this place specifically. it's big, with several different sizes of washers/driers, 2 change machines, seating, wifi, and friendly staff. the place is usually pretty busy and i see why. they also have great hours, always open when i need to wash my clothes. they also have a dry cleaner in the back which is convenient. finally, it's located right next to the tokyo food store, doggin it, and brasserie 33 in case you need asian groceries, beer, or a nice meal while your clothes are getting cleaned.

By far the cleanest and most well-maintained laundromat in the city. The people working there were constantly cleaning, readily available for assistance, and generally maintaing the superior quality of the location. It even has several television to watch while you wait. It might be a bit pricey but I'll pay it to ensure my laundry is done in quality machines without the fear of other nastiness that usually accompanies laundromats.

Clean very clean present people $2.10 for shirts and I hate doing launder at a mat but if I have to then I will do it hear.  It's worth the extra buck to do it some where thats clean has WiFi a tv for the game and is right next to a bottle shop and a bar. Ok everything is stainless.

I do wash and fold. I've never used a wash a fold service before in my life, so as far as I can tell nothing has ever been lost or damaged, things are clean, done quickly-- so for that I'd say 4 stars

BUT I would not recommend their dry cleaning. Things I've had dry cleaned there have been mis-colored, or stains remain.

Having not been to a laundromat for 35 years, I had the need to use a very large capacity washer and dryer. The employees are attentive, friendly and truly take pride in keeping this facility immaculate. The experience was painless and pleasant and I would highly recommend others to use this business.

I do my laundry here probably once a week, and this place is awesome. The people that work there are nice and it seems like every time I go someone is vacuuming or mopping so you know it's clean. They have regular sized washers and dryers but also super deluxe huge ones for the days when you need to wash everything you can get your hands on. Also, they sell individual boxes of detergent for 75 cents, which is great for whenever I forget to bring mine. The parking lot is small but there are very few times I've gone and it's been parked full (this might be different on peak days; I actively avoid doing laundry on the weekends). I consider their pricing for general laundry expensive (I believe that the smallest washers are $2.75 per load, medium - $3.75, large - $6.00, and the largest is $8.something, with the dryers mostly being six minutes for 25 cents--don't quote me on any of this, though), but it's worth it because it's such a nice place.

My first laundry experience in Pittsburgh. I was suprise when I saw this. This laundry is really clean and well managed. They have free wi fi, TV , massage chair and friendly staff. You must try. Nothing to complain about.

I have limited laundromat experience. I just moved to Pittsburgh and have not had the time or cash to buy a washer and dryer yet. I checked out Yelp and figured this was my best bet... Yelp came through once again. I got up early so that I could beat the crowd. At 9AM on a Saturday the place was pretty empty, by 10:30 it was filling up but by no means crowded - still plenty of machines left. It's clean, has free wifi, the employees seem nice enough, Crazy Mocha is a 2 minute walk down the street, prices seem reasonable considering the facilities, and clientele is not at all sketchy.

Its time to show LA la laundry factory a little love with an update because they have recently expanded. Into the rest of the building where Brasserie 23? Or was it 22 used to be. Now they have expanded spaces larger machines freedom! To do your own dance routine while your stinky socks swish to the beat in a sea of suds. 

Ok ok I know I am getting excited over something everyone hates doing, but laundry factory makes it more enjoyable. Great diversity of people watching opportunities here. There is still no bathroom but one of the laundry mistresses told me they would be getting one soon. They have drinks up front tons of change machines and some sort of card that two of the larger machines and driers take. I am not sure if you need to purchase the card to use it but seems like a laundry card you put money on. If dirty quarters drive you nuts. Great idea. 

The price is still cheaper for me than anyone else if I use large capacity washers. The beer shop.... its still awesome and its still next door. Still have free wifi and tv. 

I have never tried their drop off or dry cleaning service so I cannot review that. Just the kickass atmosphere and that I've met some pretty cool people here customers and workers alike.

Wow, what a great place. Being use to the laundromat on S. Highland and on Liberty Ave. in Bloomfield, this place is a large step up from those. I needed to wash my comforter and decided to stop in here, and I'm glad that I did. The staff were very assertive and nice, and were willing to help in any way. The facility is really nice, with a colorful industrial feel to it. Further, there are two flat screen TVs, a station for computers (with free Wifi), and even a massage chair for waiting patrons! Though I hate paying so much for doing laundry (though it's probably not significantly more expensive than places down the road), I had a very good experience here.

Oh, laundromats. How you take me back to my days in college and grad school. Though I've been fortunate to have in-home laundry capabilities everywhere I've lived over the last several years, recently I found myself in need of professional (laundry) help when my dog puked all over our comforter and mattress pad (thanks again for that, little buddy). Our washer was too small to do the job, so off I went to the Laundry Factory.

Like I said, it's been awhile since I've been to a laundromat, so I don't know what other laundromats are like these days, but wow, this one was wayyyy nicer than the ones I used to go to back in the day! It was modern, clean, bright, and had tons of well-kept machines. No dank corners where sketchy people loitered, no broken machines, no weird funky old sneaker smells. 

They had several sizes of machines to choose from, ranging from average (a regular household laundry machine) to mega-capacity. I chose the "large load" machine, which fit our comforter and mattress pad just fine. A load in the large capacity machine cost $6.00, which seemed a little steep, but not too bad. Other machines ranged in price from $2.75 to $10.00 (super mega capacity machine). They also have super capacity (50 lb.) dryers, which was very handy. It was $.50 for the first 5 minutes of drying time, and then $.25 for every 4 minutes after that. Again, seemed a little steep, but the dryers were very efficient -- I think it took only about 15 minutes (on low heat, no less) to dry my bulky items.

They had well-stocked change machines and a nice little lounge to wait in. I didn't see any bathrooms, so good thing I refrained from going to the beer store next door to have a cold one while I waited.

They do have a parking lot, but it's really small and packed, so you'll probably only get a spot if you're lucky. So plan to either park on the street or behind the building (I found plenty of space behind the building and wasn't ticketed or towed).

Anyhow, next time I need to use a large capacity washing machine (which I hope is NEVER -- hint hint, my little doggie friend), I will not hesitate to come back here.

This is the closest experience to doing laundry at home as I can get. There are a ton of washers and dryers of all sizes, (coin op so bring cash or use the ATM on location) AND a parking lot! Between 7am and 3pm the staff will give you a dollar in quarters for drying for free! You have to ask for it though. I say this is the closest thing to doing laundry at home for two reasons: free cable and byob! There are two flat screen televisions with remotes for customers to use. Free wifi and plenty of outlets for internet surfers. A bonus is the bottle shop right next door that sells snacks, drinks, and six-packs. You can even drink the beer in the laundry factory! There are two laundromats in my neighborhood but I drive 15 mins for this one because of the "perks".
This place is hands down the nicest laundromat I have ever been to. They have tons of huge washers and everything is immaculate. I will be using this laundromat exclusively.

I've put off reviewing this place for months now, which is unacceptable because I come here every weekend against my will (dirty clothing is a great motivator). Laundry Factory is located along Ellsworth Avenue next to Pitt's Dogg'n It and Tokyo Japanese Food Store. Your first impression of this place might range from "This place is clean" to "There are a lot of machines here" to "I can use my credit card to start the washer/dryer?" to "TVs?! Yes, please." Your impressions are all on point. Indeed, this laundromat is one of the cleanest I've been to. Yes, there are many machines here! Even during the busiest laundry times (the weekends), you should be able to find a machine or two that are free. Some of the larger machines accept debit/credit cards. A word of caution: for the dryers, each time you add quarters or swipe to add extra time, you will need to press "Start" or else you will lose your money. The laundromat recently attached warning labels to each applicable machine. There are two television sets, so don't worry about missing that Penguins/Steelers/Pirates game, because there is a good chance those televisions are tuned in to those games.

There is an ATM machine next to the front desk in case you are short on quarters, and the employees will gladly break your $20 bills into smaller ones. There are change machines next to the ATM machine and along the window facing Ellsworth Avenue. I counted 5-6 folding stations, which means you might have to wait or share them during the busiest laundry times.

Oh, and feel free to bring your tablet or laptop because the facility has free WiFi, which is password-protected, but you can ask any employee for it.

I didn't give the facility 5 stars because: 1, the place can get a little chaotic and very hard to navigate during its busy times, and 2, the overall cost can really add up, especially if you have lots of clothes (I don't know about what others think...perhaps I'm used to the super-cheap-economy pricing? Haha...).

Cool place, really nice attendants.  Tons of washers and dryers with a good variety of sizes.  Driers reset if you let the time run out and you have to pay the initial 50¢ again, instead of 25¢ and you only get 4 minutes for that quarter.  Parking is kind of a nightmare and there's only one entrance/exit, but only room for one car to go through at a time.  I probably won't be back.

This review is just about the dry cleaning: I was horrified!!! Maybe I got lucky living in LA having access to some incredible dry cleaning at incredible prices. I was stunned to pick up my 7 garments, paying $100 for the bill, and then going home to find cat hair and terrible ironing on my clothes. I was seriously shocked. I'm not a fan of Footer's either, but this was just so expensive it felt worse than a bad job for at least less $$.

Cool place, really nice attendants.  Tons of washers and dryers with a good variety of sizes.  Dryers reset if you let the time run out and you have to pay the initial 50¢ again, instead of 25¢ and you only get 4 minutes for that quarter.  Parking is kind of a nightmare and there's only one entrance/exit, but only room for one car to go through at a time.  I probably won't be back.

I like this place. Its one of the closest dry cleaners to my place. I have taken numerous dress shirts, silk blouses, even stained ties. 

Their service for silk shirts and dress shirts is pretty good. They tend to have the clothes when they say they will and very often they will ask you would prefer to pick up. 

The customer service has been pretty good, although it seems that they got a new register and they have been having difficulties with it because it takes them forever to run my card. 

In terms of ties they are pretty good, but I have returned home with the original stain in a tie. I have brought it back and they have retreated the tie for no charge, although they were not able to remove the stain (insert sad face here). Anyway, overall this is a pretty good neighborhood dry cleaner, they treat your stuff with care an my husbands shirts come out clean and lightly startched as I have requested them.

Clean and spacious. Someone is always cleaning/vacuuming when I'm here, and the staff are always friendly (one lady just stopped me from splitting my load in two, and showed me I could fit it all in the 80lb washer, thus saving me a few bucks!) Plenty of seating, free wifi, free parking, a tv that actually works and candy machines. Most importantly a few of the washers take card which is a godsend- it sucks to have to have to pay an ATM fee just to get change. Love this place :)

Clean and spacious. Someone is always cleaning/vacuuming when I'm here, and the staff are always friendly (one lady just stopped me from splitting my load in two, and showed me I could fit it all in the 80lb washer, thus saving me a few bucks!) Plenty of seating, free wifi, free parking, a tv that actually works and candy machines. Most importantly a few of the washers take card which is a godsend- it sucks to have to have to pay an ATM fee just to get change. Also check out the Asian market next door, they have a few unusual items to look at, like Hello Kitty water. Just be aware you have to get a bit...assertive when parking as there's limited spaces. Love this place :)

When living in a hospital, options for laundry can be limited.  The thought of a coin operated laundromat can send shivers down my spine.  Laundry Factory was suggested to us by a nurse who lives close by and it has been a life saver! 

With convenient  drop off and pick up service, I don't have to worry about leaving my wife alone in the hospital to sit and wait from some lumbering behemoth of a dryer to finally dry my clothes.  I simply stop in, let them know my detergent and softener preferences and leave as they get to work on my things.  The staff is friendly and helpful to new comers and explained the process(really simple actually) to alleviate any confusion.  The facilities looked clean and the washers and dryers looked like new.

I would highly recommend this establishment.  If you're in the area looking to do your laundry, or better yet have someone do it for you, this is the place.  I could not be happier with my results for what I think is a very reasonable price.

I sent my jacket to dry clean three weeks ago and never saw it again. I think they lost my jacket. They just keep finding excuses and trying not to be responsible for it. No one knows when it will be ready and no one knows where it is now. Everyone keeps saying "I don't know anything, but the person who knows everything is not here, please come/call later." So disappointed!!
I gave them a white blazer/jacket for a dry clean and it came back gray. Enough said.

We have a king bed comforter that needed to be laundered and is far too big for our washer! Went to the Laundry Factory based on yelp reviews. A super clean facility! All of the washers and the dryers are well maintained! I was extremely impressed!

My experience at this laundromat definitely had room for improvement. 

Pros:
-Plenty of machines
-Clean facility
-Parking
-Free wifi

Cons:
-Staff rude (see explanation below)
- No restrooms
-Credit card swipers on laundry machines unreliable

I interacted with staff to get help with a machine that wasn't working. While this staff member was helping me, a coworker came up, interrupted me, and pulled the staff member away. I waited for the staff member to return but she never did. I had to go up to the register again to be told I would just have to use a different machine. Not a big deal to move my laundry, but I the tone of the encounter was dismissive and rude. I'll be finding a different place to do laundry.

Machines are dirty. Ruined my pants and then they wanted me to pay to have it dry cleaned. Scam. They charge too much, most machines have a moldy smell and the driers apparently might have ChapStick in them according to people that work there. Don't expect any help when things get ruined. Again avoid this scamming place.

Owner is rude and condescending
Overpriced compared to other local establishments

A very uncomplicated system. You bring your dirty clothes, you clean them, you leave. However, Laundry Factory makes it an experience. Eclectic lighting, music playing in the background, places to sit and wait, friendly staff? You've got a customer for life, friend-migos.

This is simply a great place to shop, or come and just have a look!  The thing to remember is this--Eons is a very small shop and it's best to come here on a weekday when they aren't so overwhelmed.  

Like the nearby Hey Betty!, what they have here is usually first-rate.   They do NOT sell junk here (no Salvation Army Thrift Store this) but rather high quality antique clothing, many one-of-a-kind.  Like all good vintage shops, it can be a bit pricey, but if you're willing to sift and look hard, you can usually find something you want.  The clothes on their racks look clean, and are in good condition.

I'm not into vintage for everyday wear, but I play bass in a bar band and every so often I love wearing vintage clothes on stage.
i'm a total fan of eons. love their selection! a little pricey though.

oh, Eons, how you've spoiled me so.

I remember visiting Richard's shop when it was where Hey Betty! is now.  Trying on monkey fur trimmed capes and Hungarian peasant vests.  Needless to say, they know me and my chihuahua by name.

Eon's selection is amazing.  Richard is a collector, a curator, a Pittsburgh god of vintage.  He hand selects every piece in the shop and will not sell anything if a seam is ripped, a button or belt is missing, or if it's just stupid. He has every item laundered and pressed to perfection.  Everything is a gem, and Richard will tell you a bit about where he got the piece and why its design is important.  

PRICEY!?!?  gawd.  Everything at Eons is a bargain for the quality you are getting.

Growing up on Eons' vintage has spoiled me for any other vintage store.  I hold every other one up to its standards.  Thus, vintage in LA is a joke.  A cruel, un-laundered, over-priced, wrinkled, moth-eaten joke of the thrift variety.

I love the clothes he has, I love the prices, I love how helpful Richard is.  It's got a great location, and it's relative to Hey Betty!  Which is another pretty good vintage shop.  Eons is better though.  They have clothes for all sizes and shapes.  Beautiful shoes and jewelry as well.  And Richard (god of vintage) is just a gem to talk to!

I think I died and went to vintage nirvana when I stepped into Eons back in May. Every single piece is elegant, beautiful, and either close to mint condition or mint condition. Richard, the guy that runs the store, knows about every piece in the store and a bit of its history. Literally, the store is like walking into a museum of clothing from the 1940s-1980s. Hey Betty is really great too, although sometimes it doesn't have the sizes I need (I'm a petite 0-2). Also look up when you walk around the store. Some of the sweetest hats I have ever seen (I don't know where they find the stuff in that GREAT quality) are at Eons. Main point: If you love vintage, you will LOVE Eons.

You want style?  You want selection?  You want clothes that have been respectfully honored for the wearable vintage art they are?  Go here!!!  The owner Richard is top-notch and knows his stuff inside and out.   My only regret is that I didn't have more days to visit...maybe that good thing, because honestly, I don't think I would have left the store.  If I lived in Pittsburgh, I'd be making weekly (maybe even daily) journeys to the store.
I'm an experienced vintage shopper and baby - it doesn't get better than this!  And the prices - very reasonable for the quality of the clothing, which is all cleaned and tenderly loved.

This is a vintage shoppers paradise!  The place is stocked full of original vintage finds from the 1920's and on.  It may be packed full but it's easy to navigate between the different decades as they are clearly marked in select sections.  The prices aren't outrageous if you're looking for something unique for a special dinner or event.  You can tell that the owner goes above and beyond to find the best vintage selections.  It's not just clothes too, but gorgeous jewelry and a very unique selections of vintage eyewear.

This was quite the interesting find on YELP. I wanted to go to a vintage shop while in town, read several reviews & decided this was the place for me. I was beyond please! The 2 salesmen were great: personable and willing to answer questions. I purchased 2 fantastic vintage silver bangles for $8 a piece and a 50's wool hat for $10 that matches my wool coat perfectly. I wish I would have had more time, because the clothing & shoe options were amazing! I found a 20's flappers hat that I loved, but unfortunately my head is not as dainty as the women of the 20's.

Sometimes I come all the way to Pittsburgh from Akron JUST to visit Eons.  The employees are friendly & knowledgeable.  The clothing is very well organized, separated by era and then by size.  This is one of the only vintage clothing stores I've been to in the country that has a large selection of deadstock items, complete with their original tags.  The dresses I have purchased here are absolutely amazing, many of them never worn.  I will continue to visit on my quarterly P-burgh visits!

Eons was the first vintage store I ever went to at the tender age of 15 when I was going through my rockabilly phase.  I've gone back many times since, and even got my junior year homecoming dress and accessories here (it was a red '50s swing dress).  It remains the best vintage store in Pittsburgh, and possibly the best vintage place I've been to period.  

Eons carries mainly clothing, shoes, accessories and jewelry from the '40-'80s, but don't be surprised to find pieces from the very early 1900s!  It's organized by men's and women's clothing, then by type of garment, and then by size.  Speaking of sizes, there is a wide selection, which is so nice as a larger vintage-lover. Everything is in tip-top condition and very reasonably priced, and the staff are beyond helpful and knowledgeable.  I've never left empty handed at Eons, and I dare you to not find something you love!

There are thrift stores and there are vintage stores.  There are some stores that are a blend of the two.  And then there's Eons.  Eons goes beyond your average vintage shop in that it could be considered a museum of fashion.   A lot of their stuff is one-of-a kind antique clothing.  You can easily find stuff from the 1930s up to the 1980s.  Heck, in a few years we'll be looking at 1990s grunge here--time to dig out the Soundgarden CDs.  I once bought a clutch purse here.  

I stopped in the other day and even though I couldn't find anything that quite caught my eye, it was still a lot of fun poking around in here.

I lovvvvve this place. It's really well organized, employees are friendly, and I never leave without buying something. Last time I was here I got two necklaces (the jewelry is great), a quilted jacket, and a blazer with polka dot lining.

I always make a stop here when I'm back in Pittsburgh.
Meticulously organized and a great selection. Definitely worth a stop.

I have walked past this store on so many occasions, but never thought to actually walk in here until today.  Being a creature of Pittsburgh I have been doing the whole neighborhood thing.  That is to pick a neighborhood, browse almost every store in that neighborhood and then rave to everyone for about a week how great that neighborhood is for shopping.  Well this week my friends I will tell you that because of Eons, Shadyside will be spewed upon all my friends and anyone that comes my way asking where they should go to shop.

I must say, I hesitated at the door for a bit, mentally prepping myself to enter this store.  I hate when I walk into a store and cannot find anything I want.  So I prepped myself just in case that happened.  Once I walked in, I put myself at ease and just let myself browse and browse and browse.  For the small space that the store occupies, they sure do know how to jam pack all racks and shelves to the maximum.

I was greeted almost right away as soon as I walked in the door.  Of course the obligating question once you enter a clothing store of any type is, "Welcome, can I help you find anything?"  Of course I did what any typical person would do stared at them and eventually replied with, "No thank you, this is my first time in here."  I think I puzzled them with that response.  Then I just went where my mind guided me...which would have been to the shoes.  I found a swank pair of tan and white shoes that I couldn't take my eyes off of.  After about five minutes of me staring at them the guy asked me if I wanted to try them on, OF COURSE I wanted to try them on.  I wanted to hug them if I could.  Not only did he give me one shoe to try on, but unlike other places, allowed me to try the other shoe and yes, I did a little turn on the catwalk to make sure they were right for me.  And I will admit, I watched myself in the big mirror as I walked back and forth in front of it.

I also browsed a few more racks and shelves to make sure I wasn't neglecting any other items.  Good thing I did, I found the perfect vest to compliment the shoes (and once I got home I noticed it was reversible, BONUS!).

You know you had walked into an amazing business when you see that every non-filtered review here on Yelp is above par.  I'm also glad to add another one of those reviews.

Good selection, well organized, friendly staff!  

On my quest to explore Pittsburgh, I stopped by Eons and ended up trying on a few things.  I wasn't really on a quest to find anything though, but I could see myself spending hours in there shuffling through all the racks.

This place defines "vintage clothing shop". It's small, packed, and well organized. You must stop in here, even if you don't think you want vintage clothing. You will. The selection is amazing, and the staff could not be more helpful.

I love this guy! guy meaning shop owner for giving me this awesome store to stop in. Think a step up from estate sale and thrift store finds. I was able to find  a calico cotton 50's plus size dress here for my sister. 

I walked out with a 40's navy blue fitted dress with matching bolero. its super adorable! Now I just have it tailored and find an awesome full length slip to go under it. There were also some 60's Mod bubble drop earrings I really wanted but could not splurge on that day. 

He has different era's some pieces are a little pricey but most of the items are good quality. If they are damaged they are noted as damaged and priced lower.

Mostly 1960s-1980s stuff. A few pieces from the 1940s and 1950s and nothing earlier (clothes-wise anyway, they did have mesh purses from the 1920s). Lots of menswear; suits and dress shirts. The store is about half men's stuff and half women's stuff. The clothes seem to be fairly high quality (ie. not stained or ripped) but you pay for it. They did have some cute outfits, but it was priced too high for me.

A nice place to stop in if you're out for a stroll in shadyside. Though I think this place is overpriced and a bit overrated, the staff is always nice and you can discover some pretty good finds. Obviously much better for women's clothes

You simply have to visit this shop, they have the best quality vintage clothing and really excellent customer service.  The store feels cramped, but then again it is packed with a great selection of vintage clothes.  Everything is laid out very logically, and the prices are quite reasonable, especially given the quality.  

In particular, you will find a great selection of men's bow ties, and I have looked unsuccessfully for these at other stores.

One more thing, the owner supports the local community, he is continually helping out non-profits by donating or loaning merchandise and by publicizing their events.
Went in last minute for a 1975's prom theme party. Owner was very helpful and both my boyfriend and I walked out with great outfits. Didn't have to venture anywhere else!

I have never been treated so rudely in my entire life. I'm in town from Maryland trying to close my grandmothers estate and came across some vintage items. I was recommended by multiple people to take The items to Eons.  
I called made an appointment and when I arrive for my appointment Richard realize that he had double booked. I should not have been treated rudely because a mistake was made by double booking me with someone else.
 The other person that was booked with me told me that I could go first that he wasn't in a hurry. While Richard looked at my items he Was constantly saying how rushed he was and was in a complete tizzy the entire time. He then offered a small pittance for A mink stole and some handbags. I told him that I would rather donate the items to a theater.
I'm sure this store has wonderful things to purchase, but unfortunately,  because of my experience, 
will never return to the store.

I am a fan of Capristo since a co-worker introduced me to Kim Huges.  Kim is really talented, especially for blondes. She gives meticulous attention to my color and highlights.  Kim is also excellent at cutting hair.  I definitely highly recommend Kim at Capristo to anyone looking for a new salon.

I have tried many places in the past for Brazilian and other waxing, but Lydia at Capristo has it all! She is very professional while making you feel comfortable. She explains everything step by step while making you crack up. I don't think I would ever go elsewhere! She is fast and makes the whole experience almost painless! The Solon has recently been remodeled so it looks great and clean. I would recommend her to all my friends :)
Best pedicures ever.  Ask for Lydia.

I've been going to Capristo Hair Salon & Day Spa for awhile now.  From the very first moment I ever walked in there, I felt very welcome.  

Dana was my hair stylist for awhile, but now she's gone and I was wondering where she went.  I have straight hair and she was always great at giving it a more layered look.  She always knew what to do and I received complimets after getting a cut.  I liked her approach to styling my hair.  She had a wonderful personality too and a great sense of humor.  

But I'm going to be returning there soon.  They do waxes, mainicure, pedicures, and massages too.  For a trim, I'll go to Philip Pelussi--for a relaxing "me" day, I'll come to Capristo.

I went to Capristo today for the first time! I was floored by how friendly the staff were to new clients and that everyone I met knew my name by the end of my visit. I saw Kim today after reading several great reviews about her on Google search and through word of mouth, and she did NOT disappoint, friends. I went from shoulder-length layered hair into a swingy-Katie Holmes style bob with wavy curls. It looks gorgeous and I cannot wait to style it different ways. I almost want to bring my boyfriend to get his hair done, because Kim would work some GQ magic on him like faBOOSH! I will definitely be back to Capristo in the future for Wednesday martini nights. yay!

i went here to fix a bad hair cut at the last minute. I came out with a more drastic cut of the one i went in with. I was livid and called to complain. They offered me nothing. I don't recommend this salon- my stylist had no talent and no comprehension of what i wanted.

Just moved to the 'Burgh and was in search of a place to get waxed. (Italian-American...summer...get the picture?). While at MCN Salon (see my review, it's great!) I asked the stylists where to go. Nicolette said Capristo, and literally 4 other girls chimed in with "YES! See Shelly!" Darn straight: Go to Capristo, go to Shelly!

Shelly is the most efficient and speedy waxist I have EVER been to. And she's not missing stuff--she got after leg hairs and armpit hairs with tweezers. Really great job. She's a talker, which I enjoyed, as she's quite funny and kept a rolling convo going on (eases the awkwardness of being next to naked in those stupid paper panties). Was generally quite satisfied with the experience and will certainly go back.

I only gave 4 stars for 2 reasons: some of my hair has gotten quite fine from the years of waxing (not a myth! this can happen!) and ended up actually just breaking off not getting removed at the follicle. Thus the post-wax smoothness did not last as long as I would have liked. Secondly, it was pricier than I expected: $115 for lower legs, armpits and bikini. There are no discounts or package prices.

Also, beware that you can't put a tip on your credit card, so come with cash!

I went back a couple months later for a follow-up trim with Kim. Overall, my hair turned out well like last time, but she was running behind again by 30 minutes with the last girl before she got to me. The shampoo girl sprayed water in my face multiple times, and overall the service was not as good as a couple of months beforehand. I've heard more consistency about MCN salon's services and it will be at least 10-15 bucks less than what I'm paying at Capristo without the attitude. Also, the front staff is rude and needs to be polite to clients on the phone. The attitude is not worth the pricetag. Sorry.

As a disclaimer, the reason I'm writing this review is mainly selfish as I'm trying to find out what happened to the massage therapist Angie.  She used to work here, but in the months since my last massage, she's apparently left!  So if anyone knows where she is or what she's up to, please let me know!

I've also gotten a haircut here that was really disappointing given the price, but I forgive them since my hair is somewhat difficult (Asian poof).

My girlfriend and I had planned a couples massage for weeks. 1 hour before our massage the Spa called stating they wouldn't be able to do the couples massage because they made a booking error. This is after two confirmation calls previously in the week. Terrible customer service will never book with them again.

Went to Capristo for the first time yesterday and had a very positive experience. I've been looking for a new gal or guy to cut and color my hair ever since I broke up with my previous hair cutter and colorer. Actually, I didn't officially break up, I just ditched her. Callus, you say? Perhaps, but I don't always know what to do in this instance. Things go well for awhile, and then you get to a point where you feel the lovely person cutting your hair just isn't bringing it, isn't always doing exactly what you want, maybe even makes mistakes. When that happens to me I'll speak up and give it another try, but one bad haircut can make me a little nuts, and I start looking around. Perhaps you think me disloyal, but it's my hair, and I am not without a certain amount of vanity. Plus, this whole cut and color thing is costing a small fortune, so I feel justified in taking my biz elsewhere. 

I called up and asked for Sara, as someone else had posted a positive review about her. Good choice. Sara is competent, skilled and talented. She's also a very good listener. I told her my tale of woe and she came up with some suggestions and solutions that really worked. She's also got some crazy cool techniques with the scissors, and I left with exactly the head of hair that I had envisioned as perfection in my imagination. Why not then 5 stars, you ask? I'll revisit this review in the next 6 months and may up it to 5 stars, but time will tell. Hopefully the wonderfulness will continue and this will turn into a long term relationship. Yes, I'm high maintenance when it comes to my hair, thanks for noticing. 

Overall, I also like the salon itself. The women at the desk were helpful and friendly, although very busy and multi tasking, plus dealing with a computer that was going all wonky. I was offered coffee and water more than once. The coffee is good. This is a busy salon, and they seemed to be holding it together with some grace. If you park on the street you'll have to feed the meter after 2 hours, which Sara kindly did for me, as I had foil sticking up all over my head at the time. There is an adjacent lot which will cost you about $7 for 3 hours.

I've been seeing Shelly for waxes for years, and she's fantastic, totally worth the price. I've been in Pittsburgh for 6 years, and have been looking for a hair stylist that I liked and trusted ever since I moved, and Shelly recommended I try out Melissa A. I've never had so many compliments on my hair before! Gorgeous color with highlights. It's such a relief to feel like I can book a hair appointment without worrying whether I'm going to like what the stylist is going to do this time. Four stars because I had a rather pricey haircut from Roman (the owner) a while back that I wasn't all that thrilled with. He wasn't into it, he didn't ask me a lot about what I wanted or how I cared for my hair, and I left feeling like I looked like a poodle. But Melissa and Shelly are awesome. 

There are four parking spots in the lot across the street designated for Capristo customers, too, that I think many of the patrons don't know about because there's usually a spot open when I go.

I recently moved to Pittsburgh and was in serious need of an eye brow wax when I came across reviews about Shelly on the internet. My experience did not live up to my expectations at all.

I asked from the very beginning to keep them on the thicker side and bascially the same shape, only cleaned up a little. What I ended up with was one eyebrow that was thinner and shaped differently than the other. She rushed through the appt and the pricing is absolutely ridiculous for such a botched job. I could have gotten a better wax at a cheap nail salon. My eyebrow still hasn't grown back to its normal shape. And she uses strips which I think aren't as good as hard wax 

NOT worth your money!!

Sincerely,
Disappointed

I love this place.
Great front desk service, great prices and a great place for hair cuts and waxing.
If you want to get a really good short hair cut - try Sara. She is amazing with short hair. I'm very very finicky and picky about my hair but she always does a brilliant job. I totally love her. I recommended her to two of my friends for short hair cuts and they both loved her too.
For waxing - Shelly is the best hands down...Be it arms, legs, underarms or brazillian - she is quick and friendly. The best part is that she paces the service to your pain and comfort levels.

Totally recommend Sara and Shelly.

I have been going to Tom for haircuts for the last 10 years.  NEVER disappointed. Just got a massage and facial with Heather from my living social coupon and she was great!  One of the best salons in Pittsburgh by far if you're willing to pay a little extra and feel like you've earned the experience as a client of theirs.

Awesome experience. I had purchased a Livingsocial Voucher for a half-off Shellac manicure and regular pedicure. Kristy, my nail technician, was really friendly. All of the staff were genial and helpful. They weren't pushy about scheduling a next appointment or products. Overall I would definitely recommend this salon!

A friend and I bought the Living Social deal for a Shellac Manicure and regular pedicure.  We were able to get appointments close together which was a bonus.  When I arrived I don't feel I was greeted in a professional or friendly manner although they didn't have a problem with me eating a quick sushi lunch in the waiting area.

I was taken back to soak for my pedicure which was completely lackluster.  The nail tech knew I was a LS deal and I feel treated me as a lesser client.  Wouldn't you want to give better service and try to win a client for a return visit?  I left with the same calluses on my feet as I came in with.  The polish application was good though.

The shellac manicure was awful.  The application was lumpy, I had a roll on my free edge and she didn't cure my nails long enough.  A shellac mani is supposed to last 2 weeks,  I was in on Wednesday and by Saturday 2 edges had peeled off.  After 6 days I had lost 2 more nails.  I called to see if I could get a refund or a redo.  Of course the holidays were in full swing and they didn't have any appointments.  I tried calling again a couple days later and was put on hold to speak with the same person as before and was never gotten back with.

I ended up going to another salon getting my pedicure redone, soaking the shellac off and getting that redone as well.  I did not save any money since I had to pay for the services the second time, but the new salon has my business hands down.  My manisure lasted 15 days, longer if my nails hadn't grown out! Long story short dont go to Capristo for your nails!

I should probably write two reviews because I absolutely love Shelly, but Roman has now jacked up my 'do twice.  I won't be going back to see him again.  I have been a client of Shelly's for at least 4 years and have gone to Dan Cercone's barber shop up until November 2011 because I was going from a tight cut to a razored out shag and thought that using a salon would be my best option.  Using Roman was last minute and boy did I get the last minute treatment, twice.  

He has successfully screwed up my hair two times with a photo sample to follow of what I want on both trips.  Great conversation but I think he forgets what the intended goal is when someone is in his chair.

FYI: The photo attached to this account is NOT what my hair looks like now.

This place is AWFUL. I mean, so so bad. This is the 2nd time I went. The first time was awful too, but I figured I'd try again with another nail tech. Never again.

FIrst of all, the nail tech did not introduce herself, shake my hand or do anything of the sort when she came to get me from the lobby. She rushed me into picking colors for my nails and toes. Water temp on the chair got too cold too fast. Pedicure overall looks pretty good though.

The manicure is what gets me. I told her I have really oily nails so the gel polish always looks like it's grown out unless you pay special attention to putting the base coat on. She did very happily do that. However, they still look grown out - as if I'd had my nails done four days ago, not 40 minutes ago. They're also lumpy and uneven because she told me the color I picked peels from the tips so she had to put extra on... what!?  There was a chunk of dry polish on one nail I asked her to smooth and she simply sanded it with a nail file, and didn't use acetone or anything to remove the polish and repaint. so basically it looks like it chipped. My mind is blown.

At checkout, the girl was so frazzled that she repeatedly asked me "who helped you today?" "what do you need?" she seemed so bothered to have to get my coat when she insisted i give it to her when i got there. she seemed bothered to leave a tip at the desk for my tech. at one point i think she rolled her eyes at me. she was clearly stressed, so i urged her to help other clients first, but that didn't improve her attitude with helping me. 

the entire time, all the employees are there buzzing around, looking like they're stirring up drama, and not paying any attention to the clients. not to mention they all look so trashy / yinzer. at one point my tech was whispering with another stylist while doing my toes and at another point she was asking the other nail tech to send her pics from the night prior. so unprofessional.

I have one Living Social coupon left for this place ($30 for gel mani and pedi seemed like a great deal so i bought 3) but now that I've had two bad nail jobs from two different girls, I'll be asking for a refund on my 3rd coupon.

I was a first time customer today and had a great experience. The salon was nice and my stylist Chloe did an amazing job. Not only did she do a great job with my cut and color but she also went out of her way to teach me styling tips. I will definitely return to Capristos!

I just moved to Pittsburgh and was looking for a new person to cut my hair. I gave Melissa a try and I could not be happier.  She was able to see the shape and length I was after and I think she is very in tune to what the customer wants.  I was impressed by the way she listened to me and even asked questions if she wasn't sure about something.  I would give 5 stars to Melissa and 4 stars to the Salon just because I don't love the cramped layout. I would highly recommend Melissa to any guy looking for a fresh, trendy haircut.

Capristos is definitely my go-to salon. They if you want to get your hair cut or highlighted I would definitely recommend asking for Meghan- she does a phenomenal job each time. If you're in need of waxing services you should ask for Lydia :) I had a manicure done here once as well while waiting for my highlights to dry and they did a good job. It's a bit more on the expensive side than some of the other places nearby but it's convenient multitasking.

All in all the atmosphere of the place is really great. On Wednesdays they offer their customers free martinis which is an added bonus. Parking is great because the salon has spots reserved right in front of their building so don't pay for parking in the garage that's near it.

I have to admit, I don't like new people doing my hair. That combined with needing corrective coloring made me very nervous. I was pleasantly surprised , however, with my hair and the stylist! Beth is truly a master of her craft. Although she appears very young, her professionalism and knowledge far exceeds her years. She is nothing short of incredible. The prior color was supposed to be ombré , but instead was just chocolate brown with platinum tips. I was horrified, especially since I'm usually blonde. Beth was able to not only correct my color beautifully and make me a pretty honey blonde again, but gave me a product I now cannot live without. My hair is healthy, shiny, and faceted. I love it. Both Beth and her assistant are friendly and down to earth. Funny and very talkative, I almost forgot how much I hated what I came in with. It was like it never happened, and let's face it,ladies. That's what we all want is just feel good about ourselves. THANK YOU BETH!

Shelly gives the best brazilian waxes and Lydia does wonders for your eyebrows.  Shelly is quick and thorough on the bikini line.  Lydia really takes her time and shapes your eyebrows well.  I would recommend these two any time!!

I had 2 living social coupons for this spa for mani pedis that i bought so that a friend and i could go together when she was in town visiting. I called three weeks before i needed the appointments and they couldn't get us appointments together so I ended up not using them. I've called several times since then and it seems that they are always booked for mani pedis that are at the same time.  I called today 9/18 to see if i could get in to use them before they expire. They had absolutely no appointments and refused to let me use my coupons the next week though I  "could use them as gift cards and pay the difference." The lady made it sound like they were doing this as a customer service, but they are legally required to do so. Her ending the conversation with "Soo--rrrrrr-yyyyy" and hanging up didn't help the situation. Absolutely horrible customer service. Now i have 60 dollars worth of credit at a spa that I do not want to patronize.

5 stars for Lydia who does a fast, quick, and almost painless Brazilian. Even in awkward positions she made you feel comfortable. She was recommended by a friend and I would highly recommend her to others. This was my first wax and although the price tag is a little high, I won't go anywhere else to get it done.

I visited Capristo's Salon on 2/5/13 for a cut & highlights.  I was totally impressed by the Salon.  The front desk staff was super friendly.  Roman, one of the owners personally greeted me not with just a handshake but with a hug.  My appointment was with Jason.  Jason is new to Capristo's, but not to the Shadyside Hair Salon World. Jason was more than wonderful.  He is super personable, professional, and takes great pride in listening to his clients.  Prior to touching my hair, Jason sat with me to discuss what I was looking for in a cut and color. Jason specializes in a hair highlight technique that is called balayage.  I decided to try this new technique and couldn't be more happy.  My highlights are super natural looking and so beautiful.  Per Jason, balayage highlights don't need to be touched up as often as highlights.  What girl doesn't want to save money and time on looking beautiful!  My cut also turned out wonderful.  Jason spent so much time on getting to know me, my hair style, perfecting my color, as well as teaching me fun, simple hair styling tricks.  I will definately be visiting Jason at Capristo's Salon again.  I must admit that this was my absolute best experience at any hair salon!

5 stars for Lydia. She is extremely talented with wax, very professional, quick, and efficient. She is the only person I would consider going to for waxing services.
5 stars for Anita. She did my hair for my wedding day, and I am not joking when I say I got more compliments on my hair than my dress. She did all of my bridesmaids hair and my mom's hair. The 5 girls had completely different hair requests, from a fabulously big, side pony with lots of cascading curls, to a sleek chignon. They all looked fantastic and their hair really suited their personalities. My mom was my favorite of the day, she looked GORGEOUS. I can't thank Anita enough for that. She's been my hairstylist for almost 5 years now, we've done everything from long red hair, to short blonde pixie cut, Ombre, you name it, we've done it all and I've loved every style I've gotten from her. Can't recommend her enough.

I'm going to start off by saying I haven't tried any services but their waxing which is so amazing (or Shelly is anyway) this place deserves 5 stars on account of her. She is chatty and friendly which really helps since it distracts from all the pain (I'm just a wimp it's not that bad) she is inducing lol. She is really quick and does a waxing service in 15 minutes on me which has taken other professional an unreasonable 30-45 minutes?! I wish I had found her sooner because of all pain I had gone through in other salons. I know the waxing services can get pricey depending on what you get but let me tell you it is money WELL SPENT! I have been to at least 5 other salons in my neighborhood and this is by far the best.

I went to Capristo's on a friend's recommendation.  We both had bad haircuts elsewhere and needed our hair fixed.  My hair was long (below my shoulders) but layered where you could see each layer across the back - not blended at all.  I went to Roman Capristo to fix it, telling him I wanted to keep the length but clean up the layers.  Price was as I expected for a nice looking salon.  Roman was friendly and very funny but he seemed really scattered and while he listens to you in the beginning and seems to be on target when he starts, he seems to lose that focus as he continues working.

He spent a good amount of time on my hair and saw right away the error with the bad cut, explaining what should have been done, etc.  Seemed to know his stuff and I felt comfortable in the chair - until he started cutting.  He carries about 4 conversations at any time (a few of them were VERY inappropriate, especially in front of a new customer even if I am cool and can handle certain discussion).  He has an assistant for the menial tasks like washing and drying your hair - she was good.  When he was cutting though, there was almost no rhyme or reason to where his scissors went - I actually thought of him as Roman-Scissorhands because they were just moving all over my head.  In between this, he colored another woman's hair and commented when she left that it's lighter than she said she wanted but he hoped she didn't notice.  As he chopped up my hair, I wondered if he remembered that I said I wanted to keep the length.  I have very thick hair and he succeeded at thinning it out, which was needed, but it was just above my shoulders when I left - so he took the length.  The cut looked nice after it was dried and styled but once I got home and was responsible for doing it myself, it never looked like that again and now I'm noticing that my layers are even choppier and shorter on the right side than the left.  It's an improvement from the previous cut but it still isnt' great, particularly for a salon owner's work.

I called for a brow wax and they managed to fit me in an hour before they closed, this was my first time visiting this salon. Showed up (on time) I waited a while until someone finally greeted me. I was notified that the woman with whom I had an appointment with (Shelley) wasn't going to be able to do my wax and Rose took her place. 

Rose was sweet and overall, everything turned out alright. I did notice quite a few things she forgot. She didn't clean off the wax left on my face or brush away the tweezed hair.  Didn't apply any soothing lotion nor did she bother to use the magnifying light in the room! The bed was dirty too. Gross. She was clearly in a hurry. I don't anticipate going back there. 

I'm used to the amazing service I've always received from Above & Beyond Salon in Wexford. Until then, i'll continue searching for a comparable alternative here.

Super expensive but worth it. I'm pretty skittish about brazilian waxes, but Lydia is the best I've ever had. Seriously she is a goddess of Mercy. It hurt at least 50% less than usual. The place is also super clean.

I recently went to Capristo for a gel manicure and regular pedicure. I enjoy going to this salon, mostly because I can walk, but also because it feels luxurious and relaxing. I have had a massage here in the past, and also manicures and pedicures. The waiting area is roomy, and there are plenty of fun products to check out while you wait. The staff is friendly, and they do their best to accomodate your schedule.

Julie did my gel manicure and pedicure on my most recent visit, and she was fantastic. She was really lovely to talk to, and helped me to match colors and pick something that would look nice with my skin tone. I have never experienced someone so attentive in this way. Why yes, I would love a color that compliments my skin tone! 

I ended up choosing a great OPI gel color, something to do with herring... They also had the matching OPI regular polish for my toes. When you go to pick out a color, they have matching sets for your to choose from, which takes away a lot of wasted time trying to match colors. 

The pedicure chairs at Capristo are lovely and very cushion-y! It lasted for about 45 minutes, and included a nice long soak, as well as a lengthy scrub and massage. Perfectly relaxing! Julie did a great job on my nails as well, and the OPI gel lasted at least two weeks. 

The prices are expensive. You won't leave there for less than $100 (with tip), but for a luxurious treat, Capristo is a good choice.

FIVE STARS FOR LYDIA! Want a great waxing experience? Fast, easy, no pain? LYDIA is your answer! She is extremely nice and personable. When it comes to eyebrow waxing she considers what shape would be great for your face.  Bikini and Brazilian waxes are efficient and little pain. 

 I cannot express how much I recommend going to her for all your waxing needs.  Also, she gives a great facial.  I had acne going up and I went to her for facial extraction and it was great.  She was so thorough and detailed.  

Don't take my word for it? Call Capristo Salon and ask for an appointment with Lydia.  You will NOT be disappointed!

I had a sudden plan coming up for the weekend, and I realized I needed a haircut. My favorite place is MCN salon, and they were completely filled that day. Having no other option, I called up capristo and they gave me an appointment. 
The lady who did my haircut, didn't seem to be interested in my opinion and giving me something nice which I desired. I asked her to trim my layers up well, and give some shorter layers in the front. I have very dense hair, it takes some time to get the layers all done. After she cut the hair, it seemed like there was more to be done, but her next client had already arrived. She hurriedly blow dried my hair. She said, I can go back and if I don't seem to like the layers, I can come back again within a week and she will do it again for me. I was travelling after that, for some weeks so obviously didn't get to go there again.
So 1) No one has the time to go back and spend another hour getting your hair done over again 2) Everybody's hair is different, and some people's hair needs more time, so they should arrange the next client accordingly right? Instead of sending you away and asking you to come again. Plus it is pricey. ($55 for a hair cut I wasn't satisfied with). MCN salon has cheaper prices, as well as the hairdressers are more devoted :) Won't go back here again!!! :-/

Kim is the best!  I continued my quest for a hair stylist and ended up here after yelp reviews and recommendations from friends.  I started with a simple blow out and consultation regarding the hot mess which was my hair courtesy of Stonewater Salon.  She gave the best shampoo massage I have had and blew out my curly hair perfectly in no time [took 2 hours with the color consultation].  Plus my hair had body and wasn't too flat at the end.  My blow out only set me back $30 as well - awesome!

I made an appt for a relaxer the following month.  Her recommendation was for the keratin treatment instead of a relaxer to prevent further damage than what was caused by the previous color job.  It only took her 2 hours and 15 min to do the ENTIRE process and it was beautiful.  I can still walk out on a rainy day without any frizz or change in my styling over one month later and I cannot believe it.  My blow drying time has been cut in half and this is from a skeptic.  It did cost much more than the relaxer price I was expecting, but I will probably only need to do it every 4 months or so.  

The next month, I scheduled for a cut to get my layers redefined.  Again, Kim was quick and efficient.  I told her I wanted to keep my length and she respected this and somehow cut my layers to make my hair appear even longer!  This time my appt was only a little over an hour since my blow drying time was much faster.  

Since she did so well, I decided not to wait another whole month for her to fix my color.  She had earned her stripes though and I finally felt safe going under the chemical processing with Kim at the helm the following week.  I am proud to say I no longer have the tiger stripe just natural highlights as I wanted from the beginning. However, I will still need to return as I wanted more of an ombre which I cannot appreciate right now as well as a more neutral brown than auburn. Price was a little steep for not being 100% satisfied but doable.

Now I am super excited that I have found a hair stylist that can do it all - blow out, cut, color, and straightener!!  Kim, you better not retire girl!

- Only one star off for the somewhat steep (but not outrageous) for the keratin treatment, cut, and color when compared to other salons

Ok, so I really wanted to like this place. There was great parking outside and the guy on the phone was SUPER nice to me. That's about as far as it goes though. As soon as I mentioned that I use natural products on my hair, you could tell the person cutting my hair was annoyed with me. My assumption was that it was because I wasn't going to buy any of their products. Like... I've already beat cancer once.  Sorry I'm not going to put a bunch of unnecessary & cancer causing chemicals in my hair so I can go through that again just so they can make money. 

The haircut was $51. They didn't wash my hair and the haircut took about 15 minutes. I have long, very thick hair and my cuts usually take almost an hour. I tipped the stylist $10 because that's just what you do, so all in all (plus parking & the atm fee) I spent $65.50 on a 15 minute haircut in which I was made to feel questioned for my lifestyle choices. I was pretty ticked when I left, but figured they were maybe having a bad day and I'd give them a shot again next time.

Then, I went to go hang out with my best friend immediately after. She commented, "You got your haircut!," so my immediate reaction was happiness-- yayy, it's cute and someone noticed! But THEN she was like "where did you go...?" with a grimace on her face. She immediately took me to the mirror in the bathroom and showed me that my brand new, 30 minute old haircut was CROOKED. The left side was at least a quarter of an inch shorter than the right side. I would go get it fixed, but I'd be afraid they'd charge me another $50 to fix their mistake. 

So I did NOT get a good impression from this place and will not be going back.

This is actually my first post and truly warrants the review. 

I recently moved to Pittsburgh from San Francisco, CA for a job transfer.  As a female with super thick, long strawberry blonde hair, my hair stylist is more like oxygen...a necessity!   So moving across the country without knowing a soul left me to figure it out and take a chance on someone new. I bought a house in Shadyside and literally drove past the outside of the salon as I was driving around one day...I thought the exterior looked nice, clean and trendy, so I called to see if they randomly had an opening on a Saturday. By happenstance they did!  Enter game changer Amanda Radcliff!  

I had some botched up layers that hadn't be touched or cleaned up in 6 months and she worked some serious magic!  Keep in mind I have had the so called "best of the best" cut, highlight and style my hair in San Fran, LA and Beverly Hills and she, 100%, blows them out of the water. I really can't sing her praises enough. She is innovative, insanely smart and totally up to speed on trends and the latest and greatest in hair trends and techniques. Which translates to satisfied customers with the BEST hair. 

As I was sitting in her chair I sent a text to my best friend that attended the Vidal Sasson Academy of Hair in Santa Monica , CA and told her to fly out and get her hair done....no exaggeration, she's that good!  

My first appointment with her was just a cut and it was amazing!  To the point that I really didn't need to come back for several months as it grew out so beautifully. Today, she highlighted and cut my hair and it's beyond gorgeous!  

If/when I relocate for work again, she will definitely be worth the airfare back to get my hair done. I'm that convinced that she's as good as it gets!  She a MUST on your appointment list. You won't be disappointed!   Amanda Radcliff should be your next stylist!

Capristo salon is amazing.  Everyone strives to make sure you are completely satisfied and they take the time to listen.  The best is their skill at coloring your hair.  Roman the owner is excellent.  He is great at matching your hair color with skin tone etc.  I have referred many friends and they have all been satisfied.  They even ordered a wig, and then styled it for my friend going through chemo, and it was perfect - made her feel so good.  I highly recommend this salon!

I went here probably around 2 months ago and had Amanda Radcliff do my hair. I went there wanting a trim and highlights... After talking with Amanda we decided to do ombre because it was easier upkeep and would look better with the state my hair was in!! I love my hair now. It's not too crazy of an ombre either; just right. The haircut was a little over fifty dollars but totally worth it because it was one of the best haircuts I ever got. I will definitely be returning!

Worst experience ever :(  i did a hair cut and color in this salon i show her a picture of what i want and talk about the cost and every thing she told me it will cost 170 $ after we finish the hair color is soo baaaad its not even close to be acceptable she agree that i need to do it again and the same orange color tone still in my hair. after tow days working for acceptable result  i was not happy for the result she said we can't do more coz it will damage my hair .. The other shock when i saw the bill they almost double the price when i ask why??!! She told me they charge me every time she try to reach the color and fade the orange tone .. They charge me for their mistake .. I go out from this salon with bad hair color and 350 $ cost

The Capristo Salon was highly recommended by many people and just days before I left for my overseas trip I got an appointment for cut and color. I found that when entering the store, the staff was not overly friendly, but was just trying to get the job done. In that moment I didn't mind too much as I was really stressed and busy and didn't want to have small talk anyway. I was then discussing the haircut and the color with the girl and showed her heaps of pictures with the same style and also the color that I wanted to have. She then started putting foils in my hair. To have a more "natural look" she then took the "rest" of the hair and backcombed it. I asked her what this is going to be when she started as my hair is very thick and it's a pain to even brush it. But that's apparently the way they do it. 

When trying to take out the foils and wash my hair it was absolutely painful. She had to put so much conditioner in my hair and even then she couldn't just brush through it. She was so rough that I even had to stop her cause my scalp hurt so much, I couldn't handle it. The head massage was painful and rough. At that point I already wanted to leave. She then started cutting my hair and actually did a good job. I asked to cut more layers in and it was not a problem at all. Because the appointment was late at night and the light was not the best, I didn't see the color too much. However, when taking a closer look, she did the exact opposite to what I have asked for. I wanted to have foils that blend in, no thick foils and stripes. But underneath the top part of my hair I had thick very blond/too blonde stripes. Plus 2 thick stripes at the front! On top of that, the highlights dried out and are now completely strawy. I now have to let it grow out. Maybe I should have made an appointment with Kim as she seems to be the best colorist in this store. The cut was great, but the rest of the experience was just painful. I probably won't be returning for a hair appointment. I heard good things about their manicure though. But I am not rushing back.

I've been going to Capristo for awhile now, but recently changed stylists because my previous stylist left.  

I was given an appointment with Vanessa and am so, SO glad she cut my hair.  She gave me an incredible cut that has made my thick, wavy hair effortlessly chic. (Emphasis on the effortless - seriously, I can shower, throw some light product in my hair, and viola, I'm ready to go). 

She took about 7-8 inches off and used 3 different scissors to give me an individualized cut that fit my face shape and hair texture.  I'm really please with the cut she gave me and will definitely be going back to her!  

On another note - I've been going to Lydia to get my eyebrows waxed for years and she's the best in the city.  It's $25 for a wax, but trust me, it is more than worth it.  Lydia is an artist when it comes to brows!

I have only visited Capristo for waxing services, so these four stars are for Lydia. She is not only the sweetest woman, but she genuinely cares about her customers even when it's... ehhem... a bit of an intimate procedure to say the least. If you need a wax and you're in the Pittsburgh area, make an appointment with Lydia at Capristo!

Capristo Salon is my favorite! I am Miss Pennsylvania USA 2015 so it's important that my hair is looking great at all times. I use stylist Abigail Walsh for my cuts, color and blow outs before events! Julia is my go-to for my Tape In Extensions. I am so pleased and recommend everyone I know to Capristo!
LOVE Shelly! The quickest  and most quality waxes ever! Not to mention she is a sweetheart! I will be returning and sending everyone to see her!

I've been here twice in the past year, and each time I have no regrets. I first came here for a pedicure, because, you know, sandal season...and there's nothing wrong with a guy wanting his feet looking presentable! I made my appointment online on their website, which was a very simple process. A couple hours later, I received a call from them to confirm my appointment and to inform me that Kristy will be my nail technologist.

I walked in on my scheduled day. The place was definitely chic and modern. There was a waiting area in front and to the right of me; the receptionist was a short walk to the left; and there were beverages and coffee machines immediately to my left. Unsure of the protocol here, I walked past the ladies and gents in the waiting room toward the receptionist to let them know that I was present. I was greeted warmly, my name was checked off, and I was motioned to the waiting room. I sat down and waiting for only a few minutes before a staff member greeted me and escorted me to the nail stations.

As we were walking, I saw several cosmetologists working on their clients' hair while chatting and laughing away off to my left, and a hallway off to my right that probably led to the spa and laser salon treatment stations. We arrived to the nail stations, a large room in the rear right of the salon with a smaller room connected to it for pedicures. The staff member had me sit down at a pedicure station, asked me to place my feet in the warm water, and showed me how to use the massage features of the chair. While fumbling with the controls, she asked if I would like a beverage or a magazine while I wait. I thanked her but declined. She said Kristy will be with me shortly and left. After a few minutes of back vibrations, lumbar rolling, and heat, Kristy came and introduced herself. She turned on the warm water, left my feet to soak for several minutes, and one foot at a time, rubbed, scrubbed, clipped, shaped, moisturized, and polished. I declined any colors for my toenails, so I opted for a clear coat instead. The entire time, Kristy and I chatted. She was very pleasant and easy to talk with, and she definitely knew her stuff as she worked on my feet.

I came back several months later for a manicure and pedicure. Again, I was with Kristy and she seemed to remember me, which impressed me. I got a pedicure first before moving on to the manicure. As before, she was very thorough with my nails, and, again, I asked for a clear coat on my fingernails and toenails, which she gladly obliged.

My experience here has been amazing. The only negative factor is the price. Compared to other salons and spas, the prices at this place seemed to be on the higher end. Nevertheless, I believe I received my money's worth in customer service and quality. I am sure I will come back for future manicures and pedicures, and perhaps a haircut!

Wow, just spoke to someone at Capristo who was very rude. I have an Amazon Local deal that was given to me as a gift and after talking to them on the phone I decided not to go there. I think they probably treat people with these kinds of deals as second class customers.

Amazing updos / wedding hair. The hairdresser for my sister's wedding cancelled a few weeks prior and Capisto was able to get us in last-minute! I LOVED my updo and the airbrush makeup was unbelievable. Although pricey, I totally recommend it.

Ripped off. 

I just tried to use the face value of a Groupon that is past the promotional period. On the Groupon, it clearly states that the cash value is good for any goods or services offered by the vendor. Because I selected a different service they refused to honor the face value of my Groupon. The only reason I'm not still there is because it also says on the Groupon that Groupon will reimburse me if its refused. Of course, I complained to Groupon.

I moved to the Pittsburgh region to go to graduate school at Pitt. I was living in shadyside and looked online for a place that did balayage style highlights in the Pittsburgh region. There were a couple that came up but this one seemed to have really good reviews.

 I am a natural blonde ,but over the years my hair has become darker with age. I decided to try this salon because it was close within walking distance and in my budget (since I am in college). I by no means am cheap when it comes to my hair but I  cannot afford to spend 200$ every 8 weeks. After taking the time to call and confirm their price quote of 65$, which is stated online, I scheduled an appointment. 

Upon arriving I checked in and waited for a girl named Amanda. After waiting 20 minutes I was finally greated by a friendly girl and we went to discuss what I wanted done with my hair. She recommended that I get some type of highlight and also a base lift to get my roots lighter. I was also planning on getting a haircut. I then asked if what she suggested was going to cost more. It then came out that her highlights were actually going to be 95$, 20$ for this base lift treatment plus the haircut of 51$ plus tip. If I wasn't getting the base lift my roots were going to be dark which was exactly what I was trying to avoid. The total would come to around 170$ before tip. She also informed me that she was one of the lowest in price in the salon. I was very appalled that I was quoted a price and that I was not honored that price upon arriving. A 50$ difference in price is a lot of money to me when I can only work part time. 

I ended up leaving as soon as she quoted me the correct price. I felt bad that I took up Amanda's time in her schedule since she wasn't going to be making any money , but I just could not afford to do that. They might do very good work on hair, I cannot speak on that front since I left ,but I have an issue with businesses falsely advertising prices. I wasted an hour of my day to not have anything done to my hair. Thankfully I asked before getting my hair done. Be warned that you should get a correct price quote before getting anything done to your hair here. I doubt I will be giving them a second chance and I will make sure to warn people I am friends with and new to the area to not go here as well.

I would join the others & highly recommend Lydia.  I had a waxing done previously that scared me away from it but my friend recommended her & she truly does it with little pain.  She's fast & thorough.  She makes it as painless and pleasant as possible.  On top of that you get a fantastic result!  Much better than other wax only salons!  Even if you've gone elsewhere give her a try!!!
Tom is the best! My hair always comes out looking amazing! I love how friendly all of the staff is. Prices are steep but it's worth it! Definitely gonna make it back!
I went here once when I first moved to Pittsburgh. My shirts came back poorly pressed and some had broken buttons. I was disappointed.

I am not a fan of this place.  They are certainly convenient for Shadyside, and I don't think their prices are out of control.  But they do have quality issues with alterations.

I didn't have any problems with the dry cleaning, but brought some pants in to get hemmed.  First time I went back to pick them up, they told me they were out to be pressed.  Not sure why it should be sent OUT to be pressed, especially since I had come a few days later than indicated on my ticket, but OK.  Second time I come back to pick up the pants, the pins were still in the fabric - NOTHING had been done to them.  So not only were they not done, someone clearly LIED to me about where they were the first time around.  Finally got them on the third try, and I insisted on a discount.  But when I brought them home, I looked at the hem job and it was low quality.  They just flipped the fabric up and sewed along the hem, rather than tucking the cut edge under and THEN hemming.  I expected better, given the price.
I have used then for three years and found their work fine and their staff polite and even friendly. Repairs are slow but you are pre-warned

2.5 rounding up. While I'm not too thrilled with the customer service, I am content with the dry cleaning. JB & I dropped off two of his suits, two dress shirts, and our 1250 thread count Egyptian Cotton comforter on a Wednesday. We got a call on Saturday morning saying that our items were ready for pick up and my debit card was found in the pocket of one of his suits. 

(Side note: I noticed that I misplaced it 4 days prior) 

I went to pick up the items and the clerk acted surprised when I gave her 2 tickets and checked our order then told me that the dress shirts weren't ready, they were waiting for the next shipment that would probably arrive in 45 minutes. 

I told her that I'd like to pay for and pick up what was ready then made a joke about how it figures with my luck, the same day I get a call about my ATM card I get my new one in the mail. "You didn't get a call about your card?" She asked. "Yes, today" I replied. "Yeah, that was me that called, but its been here for 2 days. I can't believe no one else called". 

Because i noticed it right away and ordered a new one as soon as i possibly could, it wouldn't have mattered to me if they called sooner but if someone didn't take the proactive measures i did, those 2 days it took them to call and notify would have made a huge difference. 

The clerk proceeded to bring out the suits and cash me out when I asked her if the comforter was coming with the shirts, she then put on her surprised look again and thanked me for reminding her. She rummaged through some things and finally found my comforter and I was on my way. I'm picking up the shirts tomorrow, hopefully it wont be such an ordeal.
I went here once to get my pants hemmed and got yelled at for not purchasing proper pants in the first place. I was too startled to respond but have since thought of many  witty replies. Oh well.

Please do not give them business. Owen's has the worst customer service and quality of service. You are better off going to another nearby dry cleaner. First, they messed up one of our pants badly.
