(37.50 through AAA per person) add to that $15 parking, $58 for 3 nasty burgers and cold fries, 2 slices of pizza and 2 kids milks, $9.48 for 2 sprites and it adds up quickly. if you only want to ride roller coasters, then this is the place for you. no other entertainment was available while we were there. off season I guess. won't make the 3 hour drive again from Charleston. would rather drive a little further and go south to universal. much better value for money spent.

We went this past Sun and overall had a great time. My only issue, and why I'm on Yelp, is the food. Just horrible and way, way, way overpriced.
I would suggest spend the extra $10 for preferred parking and bring a cooler. Don't buy any food in the park. Out of desperation my sons a I had 2 slices with 2 breadsticks. Survey says-I've had MREs that tasted better.
                              Oh yeah, $14 by the way.
Preferred parking is only $10. Bring your own chow and have a great time.

Im not a rider but I love how my kids have a great time. I think their rides are great and just enough for their age range. I love how it also only takes me about ten minutes to get there. A great place to end the day with my kiddies...

It's a "good" park experience. The rides were all mostly open. The food selection was average park food. Cheese burgers. Panda Express. Rita's Ice was good. 2 new restaurants that were supposed to be open were still under construction. 
There was only 1 show open when I went cause it was early in the season. The park was mostly clean. Good amount of trees. Needs more dark rides. Cool coasters but everyone has coasters. It's also not really a theme park. It's just a good amusement park. No theming or design to take notice of. 
     But the people who work there were nice. The people who visited also seemed nice. It was a 65% positive experience. But I don't really see any reason to make a special trip as it's not really different from other cedar fair parks.
     If you are going to visit one time. I do recommend getting the "fast lane plus" option as the lines were an average of 1 hour each. Fast lane plus made everything a walk on. And front row preference on most rides.

Small park, over priced food, we paid $55 for 3 slices of pizza , 2 orders of chicken wings that were the smallest flavorless wings we have ever had, and 2 beers.....never again....pack food

Because my visit was before Labor Day the water park was closed and the park was not particularly crowded. I do think the rides should have wait times posted, though. My longest wait was thirty minutes for the Nighthawk, but if it had been busier I would have been frustrated not knowing the wait times.

The Intimidator is no joke. I *LOVE* rollercoasters, but when this one stopped, I realized my legs were shaking and I wondered what I had just put myself through. Then I put myself through it again. And again. 

The staff who run the thrill rides were incredibly professional and safety-conscious. All of the staff were very friendly and helpful.

We did the Walk with the Dinosaurs and it was pretty disappointing. The attraction is very poorly maintained. The landscaping was haphazard and all the water elements were dry, in spite of having several inches of rain the prior week. Definitely skip paying the extra fee for this.

Let's start with an explanation of my once BAD review.  One of the employees at the water park, without explanation, told my 13-year-old daughter to "take off your shirt" at one of the water slides.  It was supposed to be a precaution, which is not located on any signage on the ride, but my daughter had been on that ride numerous times in the same outfit and never had an issue; it didn't help that the boy followed her to the pool right afterward.  She was scared to death!  So I went to Carowinds infuriated.  The first two people to take our complaint basically patted us both on the head and sent us on our way.  WRONG!  

Thankfully, a gentleman named Jerry met with us the next day, because I was seriously plotting an "accidental" mishap of one water slide employee down a nice, high flight of steps.  He took our complaint seriously, made sure it was handled the way it should have been handled and asked us to come back to the park so he could talk to my daughter and make her feel more comfortable about returning.  Ninety minutes later my daughter is feeling a lot less stressed, a LOT more comfortable and she has two new friends at the park who have her back.  Having this situation happen in the first place was a seriously bad scene, but I now have proof that the higher ups at Carowinds take this behavior just as seriously as we do, and it's not going to happen again.

UPDATE:  That nice guy Jerry?  Just another CS liar.  Promised to make my daughter happy with future Carowinds experiences and reneged on every single promise.  Not happy with this place.  They won't be getting our money next year, no matter what the "big plans" are, and they got six season passes out of us!  We're officially done with Carowinds.  Saving up that six hundred bucks to go ELSEWHERE.

As a kid I remeber fallong down an open unmarked manhole, and not getting anything save a change of clothes and a freaking lollipop, they also refused to do anymore to compensate me. This also wasn't an emptied manhole, it was nearly overflowing. I will never go back to this park since this happened, and the lack of proper response.

It's Carowinds. Some good rides. Most surrounded by stuff you won't ride or games you won't waste money on. The kids will have fun, no doubt. The people are nice enough. The group hospitality is very good with great brisket and chicken. They make you feel welcome. Just enjoy it.

If you want a one-liner, I had a really great time here with my friends and wife, but I do not think that Carowinds is a great theme park.

Tickets - Just like department stores, Carowinds largely overprices its tickets at the door ($55?) but has numerous gimmicky sales. For example, going to Bojangles can get you $15 off.  Various schools and hospitals have various discounts ranging from 50% off to only $10 off. You'll never feel like you got a good deal.

Parking - Preferred parking is $25 while standard parking is $15.  Preferred parking is basically designed for families that want to eat outside of the park for lunch or dinner and I would recommend it if you plan on coming in and out of the park.

Weather - It rained just an hour after we arrived here. There are no rain checks or refunds. Most of the rides shut down until a good 30 minutes after the sun started shining. It can really put a damper on your day.

Rides - There are some pretty good rides and some really, really bad rides.  The log-ride is literally one slope.  Literally one.  If you don't know this beforehand, you might wait an hour to experience about 15 seconds of ride.  Drop-zone (I forget its new name) is literally one free fall for a couple of seconds.  Do not waste your time on these two rides. Good rides include The Intimidator and After-Burn which are both quite impressive.  You can expect to wait quite a long time for each of them but I would recommend waiting for a front-seat on each of them.  It's really a great experience to see the entire park from the top of the coaster and you really do get a great sense of flying on After-Burn. 

One thing that really bothered me about some of the rides is that no one cleans the restraints, especially the overhead bars, and as a result, it's stained with the odor, oils and dirt of thousands of riders before you. As a result, my experience on Night-Hawk was not quite as pleasant as I would have liked. In addition, somebody should tell the ride operators that there is no need to speak loudly into the microphones because most of the time they're painfully loud and the speakers are distorting.

Food - $10 minimum for any main entrée, $4 for drinks, everything will gouge you. They don't allow ANY outside food or drinks. Prepare your wallets.

Extras - The dinosaur park is $2.50/person for groups of 4 and it was kinda nice, but you have to really like reading (there's a LOT to read) and learning to get the most out of it.  The 3D movie about dinosaurs is included but it's kind of depressing, and doesn't have the cool gimmicks like moving seats or mist that Star Tours or Honey I Shrunk The Audience had. 

In conclusion, I actually had a great time at the theme park with my friends and wife, mostly because we luckily came to the park on a Sunday that apparently wasn't very popular and thus didn't have to wait very long on any lines.  Had we come on a "normal" day, I probably would have been a little bit less happy.

DO NOT BUY THE MEAL DEAL AT THE PARK OR ONLINE. I REPEAT DO NOT BUY THE MEAL DEAL.  At 30 bucks a person YOU think it will save on eating costs. ..NOPE you get 5 places to eat at and YOU do not get to choose what you eat the employee failed to mention this. NO healthy coices from the 4 things you can eat and DRINKS not included. Carowinds made 20 bucks off us cause after 2 meals each of crap pizza and nasty "chicken" fingers we gave up. DO NOT FALL FOR IT. Otherwise it is an amusement park full of wild children and crazy pushing people. Not like I remembered as a kid. Prepare to see a chiropractor cause rides are old or whiplash causing. The intimadator bout killed me whoa. Employees were nice cept for meal deal scam lack of information kid. And the park restrooms  WERE A NIGHTMARE. So nasty. Save your money go to Dollywood way nicer crowd and their meal deals have real food  choices. Thanks Carowinds but never NEVER again.

Carowinds is a wonderful amusement park and water park.  It is small enough that you can ride every ride in one day and large enough so you are never bored. Buying a Gold Season Pass is the way to go.  After 2 visits you have gotten your money's worth. Parking is free with the season pass, otherwise it is $15 each trip.  Carowinds has many trees and flowering plants everywhere.  Very easy to be in the shade when the sun gets too hot.   It is wonderful to have such a nice park here in the Carolina's!  Living close allows us to go there anytime we want, like having a theme park in our backyard!

Great all in one theme park! Ideal place for both kids and adults. I love that there are still remnants of the old Carowinds when it used to be owned by paramount. The water park is a nice place to stay for the whole day, especially once the two new slides open up. Carowinds also provides job opportunities for young teenagers starting at the age of 15! Most of the employees are relatively friendly except for the Wings restaurant. Everyone is grumpy there. But at least they give a good amount of fries. Wish I had more time to experience the WHOLE park! I went from 11-7 and only got through 3/4 of the park. (Note: rode The Intimidator twice within 20min)

If you are planning to go more than three times, just get a gold pass.  The amount you will save on parking alone is worth it.  
The best time to go is during the weekdays, and get their early.  You get better parking, and get in early.  Food is over priced, just bring a bottle of water in with you and fill it up at a water fountain.  Boomerang Bay is a great get away from the park, and you must ride the super tall water slide!  

The rides are fun.  My favorite is the intimidator, and the wait is not to awful bad, they added another cart this year.  Dropzone is fun to ride if their isn't a wait, otherwise, don't waste your time.  Carolina Cobra is fun, and the wait is not usually that long.  Vortex is fun as well.  Just plan to spend a day out here.  

FYI: The all day dining pass dose not include any drinks at all, and is hardly accepeted at places in the park.

Haven't been here in yeaaarrss. Had a good time, although the tickets were very expensive compared to other theme parks I have been to. Rides were pretty fun, and the lines were very short the day that we went. Enjoyed my time, will come back if in the area again.

Great rides! I have always loved carowinds. I like it better than universal studios. I think the rides are better at carowinds. The only thing is they are a little pricey but they do run deals sometimes. Most amusement parks are pricey anyway. I'll definitely be back!

I have a love/hate relationship with Carowinds.I do not like Carowinds (hate is such a strong word after all) and my children love it. What's a parent to do? Buy everyone season passes except yourself. Problem solved. Walking around in extreme temperatures having your flesh seared by the sun, waiting in long lines and looking at large people in tight clothes/bathing suits is not my cup of tea.
The positives:1) the Snoopy World is awesome for the little ones, 2) if you love roller coasters, I think they have about eight of them, 3) season passes are actually affordable, 4) some of the food is actually not bad.
The negatives: 1) if you don't like roller coasters, or water parks, there's not much else to do 2) the place is packed on weekends (when people with jobs can actually go), 3) the food is way over priced.
The negatives and positives kinda balance each other out. The best part is watching your children smile and have fun (in between heavy applications of sunscreen). The best part for me was at Harmony Hall. A large air conditioned food court where live bands play. Yes my brisket platter was $14, but it was good brisket (and almost a pound). My sides of mac and cheese and baked beans were high quality product. I was so suprised by the quality I forgot all about the price. And raspberry Coke is pretty awesome.

Went today for the first time in a long time.  Not as great as I remember but definitely worth it.  There were quite of bit of rides.  We are traveling and there is a kennel for the dog.  The price was 10 dollars for the dog you jave to walk it and feed it but they will give it water.  The pens are small for large dogs, we own a German Shepherd that weighs around 85 pounds.  Though small she was able to stand up in it just not move around alot.    The cost of the park was 57 dollars if bought at the park if you buy online you could save yourself some money.

If you have been to Disney or even Chi-fil-a this place will disappoint you with their horrible customer service. Perhaps when 80% of your staff are 18 yrs and younger you need to instill respect, courtesy and the customer is always right b/c they just dropped a freakin mini fortune on this crappy amusement park that post hours of operations for stores and restaurants as suggested times. And you only get 1 star because I couldn't leave it blank

I like Carowinds, my kids have fun and we have season passes.  I am yet to make it to the Halloween Scarowinds but heard that was the best.  The waterpark is cool.  My only complaint is it is very pricy.  I think it's like $4.00 for a bottle of water. you can't bring your own food in there. One time we went there and rented a carriage and got some drinks and my husband said, "we already spent $400.00 and we are not even in the main park yet!  so beware of the money situation!

Stopped by Carowinds on our 5 park, 4 day, Fourth of July weekend! I'm from Cincinnati, Ohio- born and raised so my Platinum Pass for Kings Island gets me into Cedar Point and other parks for no charge. Carowinds is one of those.

I enjoyed my visit here and they've got some real good coasters. Intimidator and Afterburn were my top coasters here, but there are some classics such as Carolina Goldrusher and Thunder Road. I can't wait to see the coaster going in next year. If it's what I'm hearing you all are in for a treat- the track is coming from right near my house so I hope it's what I'm thinking. 

Definitely stop in if you are in the area. I will be back at some point!

If your coming here BUY THE TICKETS ONLINE, you will save $5-8. Also come here EARLY. Like any theme park they nickel and dime you for everything. General parking was $15. Tickets were $48 (online discount). Water was $4 for a small bottle. I would advice anyone to purchase the theme park water bottle for $15, share it and receive unlimited refills throughout the day. Each rides wait averages around 40min-1.5 hr wait. Realistically, you will get through 1 ride per hour unless you have a fast track pass which costs $55 for 12 fast track passes. If you actually get to the roller coaster its well worth it. The intimater was a bit daughnting yet exhilarating. The night owl gave a different perspective view when riding the roller coaster because you a laying down. Overall this place is ok. Due to the location of this place it gets extremely hot and the wait can become unbearable. I do not think i would come back to this place again due to the heat and overall priced things as other amusement parks at least offer combination packages that are more affordable. Cheers!

Don't come here if your Body Mass Index is anywhere above perfect; I have a 40" pant size and cannot fit into any of the roller coaster seats.

Upon complaint management would only refund half my ticket cost, evidently it's worth money to wait in like to be told you're too fat to ride.

Had our bags stolen when we were required to leave them in unattended cubbies to go  on a ride. Park was beyond rude and unhelpful about it. Food is expensive and nasty. Make sure you put your things in a locker since the park does not watch or care about your belongings. If the park is demanding you leave your belongings, they should figure out how to keep it safe.

Decent regional amusement park... Quick turn around on some of the rides... Not so much on some of the others. Intimidator had the fastest turn around today... We averaged 10-15 minutes in line... Through 3 visits.  

There were enough rides to keep my 4 y/o occupied. A fair amount that we could ride together as a family.

  Food... Ugh overpriced as per the norm. Mostly burgers, dogs, pretzels, funnel cake and a Panda Express.  Buy the premium parking and eat off the park, you'll thank me later.

GREAT TIP ENCLOSED: Overall, like this park. It's older, but still fun. I am much happier now that they offer a fast-pass lane. Waiting in lines (at any park) is horrible on a hot day. You would otherwise wait for a good 2 hours for the most popular rides. Two hours for a 1-2 minute ride, no thanks! There are plenty of restrooms throughout and food options.

TIP (the best tip you can ever get here): go to ANY concession stand (that has a fountain) and ask for a COMPLIMENTARY ICE WATER. For liability and your safety, they're obligated to provide guests with water so they stay cool and hydrated. You won't really find any drinking fountains, and unless you want to pay something like $5 per bottle of water, this will make your experience MUCH more pleasant!

My wife and I showed up the other weekend and got stuck on one of your rides that you lay down on. We we're stuck laying down tilted back on this roller coaster for about 20 minutes. Everyone on the ride was flipping out because we were all getting head rush. When we finally got off after your employees gave zero communication. We were told that if we would of shut up and listened we would of known that there were technical difficulties. Seriously who says that?

The medics there did nothing but give us a cup of water. After sitting my wife down for an hour to rest she actually became sick and was on the verge of passing out and all you guys could do was give her a free drink. 

Over 100$ worth of money spent to only have been there for a little over an hour. It was a waste of my day time and money. It was my wife's birthday and instead of being able to enjoy the day we had to leave because of the issues from the ride malfunctioning. A day looking forward to having some fun turns into a damn headache. It's sad when a park can only give you a drink for compensation.

I was immediately impressed by the overall cleanliness of the park.  The rides and shops looked practically new.  After having worked at an amusement park in TX, I was very shocked at how clean the park looked.
The only problem was that the restrooms were disgusting.  The smell was so horrendous, I had to hold my nose in order for my gag reflex to subside.
The rides were amazing and I liked that the park had a Peanut section for younger children.
My kids had a blast, we will return!!!

My wife and I bought tickets online in advance to the park. We came on Halloween night for Scarowinds. Well we were here for 30 minutes before rain and lightning came. We went to guest services and they told us there are no refunds. If you plan on going to this park make sure to check the weather or kiss your $$ goodbye.

It is about in between a Six Flags and a Disney park on a scale of how nice it is. Nice selection of coasters, but the park layout is kind of all over the place. It is a lot like King's Island in Ohio although I would say King's Island definitely has the winning edge. Favorite coasters were Intimidator and Afterburn.
Since my last review I have been to Scarowinds, the BEST, realistic scary experience ever and the lines go fast!  I will go every year and I LOVE HALLOWEEN!!!

The theme park of the Carolina's that is made for each member of the whole family. They always have new rides every year. Always check out the Sky tower when you check this place out. It may not be Six Flags or Disney world but it is a lot of fun. Its opened from March till November.

It is a re really great place to go out for a day and just enjoy the thrills of each ride. They have rides that are suitable for all ages and for all types of thrill seekers, especially witht he new introduction of the worlds tallest roller coaster,  the Fury 325. And with the edition of of a water park, it is great for having a nice day for the family and having a splash.

Clean park, friendly and helpful personnel. Great rides. That  being said, I spent 2 hours in line for intimidator and over 3 hours for Fury. That just about shot our day. Surprised at how bumpy and shaky the Fury was, expected a much smoother ride. Food was good, but lines are too long for 65 year old with bad feet. Today was sunny with temps at 81. Thank goodness for stiff  breezes and intermittant shade or I would have had to drop out of line. Might have to by pass these two headliner rides next trip. I had  my shirt pocket bottoned down but came open during Fury run and my small credit  card holder flew out near end of ride. Very helpful employees checked accessible area and found it, very grateful and thankful for retrieval. Will be back but may take some time.

Carowinds has done a really great job of improvements the past few years. With the expansion of the water park, the addition of a hyper and a giga coaster, the addition of Harmony Hall, and a complete overhaul of the front of the park, Carowinds has transformed into an elite theme park.

I've always found the employees at Carowinds to be great. They're always smiling and some of the ride operators have a great time interacting with the riders. A few years ago on Vortex, the ride op would say "Thank you for shopping at Wal-Mart!" or some other silly phrase when you got off the ride which just made the experience that much better.

Ride reviews:

Intimidator--Great hypercoaster with lots of airtime and a fantastic train layout. 5/5

Vortex--Also known as the nut crusher, this one can hurt, especially if you have to wait at the end for the next train to load. 2/5

Carolina Cyclone--Uncomfortable and headache inducing. 2/5

Thunder Road--A racing wooden coaster which has been partially retracted. Some of it is still very rough but not to the point where you'll get hurt. 3.5/5

Hurler--Another wooden coaster, slightly better than Thunder Road. This one has been partially retracted as well but some parts still hurt your outer leg as it hits the side of the lap restraint. 4/5

Carolina Goldrusher--A kids' double chain lift rollercoaster. It's actually pretty fun, even for adults but the line moves unbearably slow. 3.5/5

Fury325--Takes the cake as the best rollercoaster I have ever been on. Lightning fast and extremely intense, just a fantastic ride. 5/5

Carolina Cobra--A boomerang coaster that will give you a headache. 2/5

Nighthawk--One of the few flying coasters left. The line moves slow and it breaks down often, but it's a really cool experience to feel like you're flying. Don't ride it if you're claustrophobic. 3.5/5

Haven't been here since 1999. Some things have changed for the better, some not so much.  The front of the park looks great.  Hopefully, the rest of the park can get the special updates; it's showing its age toward the back.

 Fury 325 was an great experience once we got past the 3+ hour wait. I imagine it's just going to be worse the rest of the season.   For a smallish amusement park, there are enough thrills and chills to satisfy.  Be prepared to spend plenty for food - as typical, no deals there.  Decent variety and even a couple places with alcohol.  I think the next time I go, it will be on a weekday, nonpeak.  See you after Labor Day!

I cannot say I have ever had so much fun at an amusement park.  Now, the company was amazing as well.  Let me tell you, the selection of roller coasters and rides in incredible.  Fury 325 opened last week, so we had to experience this.  It is the worlds highest and fastest (95 MPH) giga coasters in the world.  It was so worth the 1 1/2 hour wait.  If you have been to Carowinds, take Afterburn and the Intimidator (Dale Earnhardt Ride) and fuse them together and you get Fury.  It was fast, smooth, heart-pounding and insane.  

The swing that goes high above the park at sunset is so relaxing.

Add a few Peanuts rides and a Merry-Go-Round with cotton candy, pretzels and people watching to your heart's content and you have a great time.

Don't let Ricochet fool you.  It may look like a kids ride, but it is fun, fun, fun.

Batman shirts beat Superman shirts.  If you decide you want a game to play at the park.

Go early at park open.  You will spend an entire day there.

P.S.  Daily tickets are 59.99 (49.99 if you buy them online at the Carowinds website).  If you have a AAA membership, go to a local office in Charlotte.  They are $38.00.

Parking for the day is $15.00.

FURY 325
We went to this park yesterday to ride Fury 325. We got there when the park opened and went straight to the ride. It took 40 min for them to open the ride because of frost on the tracks. (**This isn't a complaint -- just a fact**) The line was very well managed and everyone was patient and excited. We all cheered for the first car of people and it was awesome.

Once the ride opened, it only took about 40 min for us to get to ride. The operators are EXPERTS at getting the train loaded quickly, and they ran all three trains. We went back twice later, and each time was only a 30 min wait time. Awesome.

The ride experience was unparalleled. I was initially nervous about the lack of shoulder harness for the 81 degree plummeted, but I felt really safe with just the lap bar and seat belt. The ride was smooth, even careening through curves and under the Carowinds entrance way.

Got front row once - definitely felt smoother and faster than the other parts of the train.

World Class Coaster. Go now.

EVERYTHING ELSE

Water -- several defunct water fountains, $4 for a bottle... this part sucked. I went to Busch Gardens last week, and there were water fountains everywhere. Carowinds, take care of your guests and install some fountains.

Food -- expensive and disgusting. We went to a place that advertised having veggie burgers (I'm a vegetarian), but they were out. I got a $10 cheese pizza and a breadstick that was really just flavorless bread. I wanted coffee, but they "hadn't made any that morning." Yep... they said that. Duuuude.

Service -- it's early in the season, so the operators are still having a blast and acting hilarious. I loved everyone on the Rapids ride, the girls on Thunder Road who were going back and forth, and of course the efficient team on Fury. The Cinnabon, however, was understaffed with only one young girl to serve and act as cashier... I guess her manager had stepped out? 

------------

Worth the trip, but pack a picnic lunch and tailgate.

In the world of amusement parks you've got kiddie parks, theme parks (Disney-Universal) and then your traditional park which is what Carowinds falls under.  But what makes Carowinds special are its two thrill rollercoasters, Fury 325 and the Intimidator.  So of course I had to make the drive down to Charlotte and check em out.

Carowinds is thankfully reasonably priced at $42/ticket for the early season.  $15 for parking and then in we go.  There was a fast pass option which we declined and we immediately jumped on the two main coasters.  Wait time was approximately 90 - 120 mins which was tough but both these rides were GOOD!  We also tried two other coasters which were decent but it was all downhill after the first two.

Carowinds has decent food options with most meals (burger-fries, chicken-fries) going for $14.29 and then beers at $8.  Pricey but about par for the course.  Due to the early season the water park was closed so we couldn't have any fun there.  Overall I think Carowinds is decent but a bit small and limited for rides.  Their top two coasters are worth 4 - 5 stars but taken as a whole, there's still some more renovation needed here to bump it up to the top...

Like all amusement parks, the tickets, parking and food prices are insanely high. However, it's not worth it here. We visited during the week in the Spring, and were pleased with the size of the crowd- however, Carowinds also understaffs during this time. They only had one employee working each ride- so the one person was doing the job that 4-5 employees could have done to make the lines move quickly. It took 5-7 minutes to load and unload each 30 second ride. Hours of waiting in lines, especially for kiddie rides, is unacceptable. There s not much to do aside from the rides for young kids- unless you pay extra for entertainment- and the layout of the park is terribly confusing and poorly planned. The water rides were not in operation either- which should have been reflected on their website. Due to the complete lack of water fountains, you are left to buy the $4 bottle of water. It is a clean park and the employees are generally friendly- although when we stopped at a 'help' spot to find out what rides we could do with our 2 year old, the employee was clueless. We won't be returning.

What a fun way to spend a few hours a few times during the summer.  Make sure to buy a pass though since it pays for itself in 2 visits and parking is free with gold passes.  Scarowinds is also included with the gold pass and that is a blast to ride the rides late at night with a few haunted trails mixed in.  Make sure to eat before you come or you will shell out $30 or so for chicken tenders, fries, and a drink for two people.  The new Fury 325 ride is awesome.  I have never been on anything so fast before in my life.  Bring a couple dollar bills since the new ride has 0 cubbies for you to put your bag or things in when you get on the ride.  They make you rent a locker for that ride.  Once you get going down the hill all your worries will disappear.  My favorite ride is still the Intimidator.  Great fun, but remember, BUY THE PASS BEFORE YOU GO!!!!!!!!

If you have been to any Disney Park this is a complete and utter disappointment. The "fast pass lane" is nice if you'd like to add another $75 to your $60 admission price. All staff seem to be teenagers who are rude, disrespectful and try to go as slow as possible. It took one kid 5 minutes to refill our drink. The rides are decent, but not worth the 2 hour waits. We were there for 8 hours and rode 4 rides after deciding not to purchase the $75 fast pass. Overall Carowinds was a large waste of money & an extreme disappointment for the Carolinas in general. My boyfriend looked at me and said "this is why no one ever talks about Carowinds. It's miserable." We will definitely not be going back.

My husband and I live in central North Carolina, but traveled to Charlotte for a long weekend to explore uptown Charlotte and Carowinds.  Since we're only about a 2 hours' drive we decided to get season passes, which included our admission on both Friday and Saturday, parking on both days, and 10% off on food in the park.  Even if we don't return, it was slighly cheaper than paying a la carte for tickets, parking, etc.

We also bought the fast passes for Friday, because we just really don't like to stand in line.  I figure it's already expensive, so you might as well pay a little more and get the most out of your time.  Looking back I'm so glad we bought them because Friday was a beautiful day so the park was packed!  But with our wristbands, we never waited more than 5 minutes to get on any ride.  They even asked us where we would prefer to be seated on the roller coasters, which was awesome.  We ended up riding every single roller coaster at least once.  We rode Fury 3 times in 15-20 minutes.  For lunch we split a $10 pizza and a bread stick and had a drink at the bar.  If you eat before you go and as soon as you leave you can get by with sharing something small instead of paying $16pp for a hamburger and fries.

When we returned on Saturday we didn't buy the fast passes because we planned on walking around and sampling the food from the food festival.  However, it was an ugly day and when we got there around noon there were absolutely no lines for any of the rides.  We rode the intimidator 3 times in a row as soon as we walked in, just like we would have done if we had purchased the fast passes.  After that, we just walked around and shared the tasting plates from some of the various regional food booths. I  was so surprised to see that we were literally the only ones participating in the food festival.  I couldn't believe that there was a line at Panda express and that the booths where you could get $4 tasting plates, beers, and wines were empty.  To each his own, I guess.  

Anyway, we had a great time and will definitely go back since we have the season passes.  My only piece of advice is if you don't want to shell out the money for the fast passes then make sure you go on a rainy day, unless you enjoy standing in 2 hour long lines.

I visited Carowinds on Saturday May 10th - it was graduation weekend for many of the universities in the area and Mother's day the next day. My friends and I weren't sure what to expect with the crowds but it ended up being a perfect day. Our average wait time for any ride was about 45-60 minutes. 

They really have a great variety of roller coasters - lap bar (Intimidator, Fury 325), shoulder bar (Carolina Cyclone, Carolina Cobra), stand up (Vortex), laying (Nighthawk), dangly feet (After Burn), and wooden (Hurler, Thunder Road). It was nice that we never really felt like we were going on the same ride over and over again. 

The new giga coaster Fury 325 is an awesome ride! It was the only coaster that we went on twice during the day. This ride is brand new this year and unlike the other coasters where you bring your belongings with you and place them in a bin, this ride does not have the bins. Instead they have lockers that you rent - SCAM TO EARN MORE MONEY! The locker costs $1/hour with a 2 hour minimum. The only plus side to this method opposed to the bin system is that they unload and load that ride SUPER fast so even a long line moves pretty quickly. 

The food offerings are pretty standard for an amusement park - lots of hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, chicken fingers, french fries, pretzels, funnel cakes, etc.

The park itself could probably use a few improvements like new paint on some of the rides - which I thought maybe would have been done in the off season every year. 

My biggest complaint from my trip to Carowinds would be the fact there are ZERO signs around the park to point you in the direction of a certain ride you may be looking for. In every other amusement park that I have ever visited they always have tons of huge signs or "street signs" pointing in multiple directions for all of the different attractions. They have maps at the entrance so be sure to grab one.

Really disappointed,  first I spent the extra money for the special parking but it was no where to be found i even asked security where it was at he had no clue likely it wasn't super crowded.  Then we paid and we attempted to go on multiple rides but half of the rides were down.  Every person that works here is about 18 and under I swear they are all young and they are rude no professionalism what so ever at one point they were arguing over the microphone.  I would never come back here I'll stick with six flags

During Memorial Day weekend. We waited 2 hours in line to get tickets as service member we can only get online at a certain ticket booth which services season passes, online passes, refunds. No one at the park cared that there were so many people online instead of designating a line for certain things. Nope! After drive 4 hours to come here I will never come back nor refer anyone else. Oh and we needed a wheel chair they had none available because people had them in the parking lots when they not supposed to leave the park with them. And they had no idea who let them leave the park. Customer service (this includes supervisors & managers)....

I am from Florida and will always be a Disney kid at heart. However, I now live in NC and on a 3 day holiday weekend I was more than willing to try Carowinds as a replacement to that void. Sadly, I was not that impressed. 
First off, the park admission is pretty cheap currently and I found a deal online that offered free parking, so I was happy with that. We also knew that going on a holiday weekend we'd be in for long lines, so after attempting a 2 hour wait at Afterburn, we cut our losses and bought the Fastpass tickets- highly recommended during these kind of days!! The longest wait we had at any ride from that point on was maybe 15 minutes.  
Unfortunately the park itself was rather lacking. There is no theme or reasoning to how the park is laid out, kind of reminded me of a beginner playing Roller Coaster Tycoon. Sure let's put a Chik Fil A next to a kiddie 3D haunted house, which is next to a reverse level 5 coaster! Also, I noticed that everywhere we walked there were chain link fences which really just seemed unprofessional, almost like I was in a carnival for a church fundraiser. One of the fast pass lanes went under the roller coaster and with the chain link fences everywhere, no lighting, and no person to guide you,  we felt like we were about to be mugged. 
Food cost was insane; We're talking 4 dollars for a bottle of water! Also, absolutely no exceptions for food or drink being brought into the park. They checked all bags too so good luck smuggling anything-  Disney isn't even as expensive and strict, at least they'll let you bring in little baggies of food, buying snacks for a bunch of kids can add up, especially considering the fact that there aren't that many healthy options. There's a marketplace in the front with fresh fruit but that's it; no worries though, you'll find a churro or funnel cake stand every 5 feet! At one point, we stamped ourselves out and went to the car for snacks which is just so stupid. We did eat at the marketplace mentioned earlier, but oh boy, there are people yelling at you to know what you want, where to go and don't walk in until you're 100% sure. I wanted a panini and surprise the machines weren't turned on (it was 1pm). Myself and one other person stood there for 20 minutes before we suggested just tossing our sandwiches into an oven. The kid had to ask for permission from a manager to do so! We both ended up with cold sandwiches and not even so much as a "sorry for the inconvenience" from the manager. 
The only theme we seemed to notice at this place was a lack of communication from the crew. All of the employees looked under 18 and probably here as a part-time job. Zero smiles, cashiers just standing at registers with a line out the door, difficulties with locking up cubbies before boarding a ride, no one guiding anyone through turn styles (the big rides had people, but often, it was just a free for all boarding which caused chaos in lines) and even on one roller coaster, they were so rushed to get people locked and loaded, nobody walked by to ensure my belt and restraint was on properly! Obviously I survived but I have never been so terrified on a ride before! 
Lastly was the rides themselves. This is an extreme coaster park, so be prepared for just that. Aside from the 3D boo blasters ( mind you, they want you to pay for the glasses and if you don't, you just don't get to play the ride in 3D!) and indoor music theater, every other ride is high or fast, so this is certainly not a park for young kids. The wind seeker (yo-yo?) ended up being my favorite ride because it was high, awesome view, and didn't hurt my head. All the other roller coasters caused my neck and head to scream with pain; For the record I'm 29 so I'm not exactly old. The Fury, their newest roller coaster, had a G force so extreme that after the initial fall, during the pull back up, I actually lost partial vision from the blood rush. That may seem awesome to some people but it was pretty damn scary to me. I noticed on several rides about half a dozen people not able to fit. Most of these people weren't even that obese- my husband at 220lbs found himself rather cramped on the wooden rides which makes me wonder, when we live in one of the world's most overweight countries, what weight do they expect people to be?? Just a heads up for anyone who is carrying a little extra baggage to be warned, these seats seem to be very small. 
We wanted to rest our heads so we decided to go to the outdoor theater, only to be informed that this was an extra fee. I'm not a fan of a park that requires additional pay for something like live music that occurs throughout the day. 
A strange layout, rickety rides that make your head feel like a washing machine on the spin cycle, total lack of care and communication with workers and extremely overpriced meals, I really can't say I had a fun day at Carowinds. Next time we venture outside, we'll go north and try Busch Gardens in Williamsburg, VA.
Brought my family here and it was a lot of fun.  I did not have any expectations. Our 5 year old stayed busy & entertained. The water park especially made a hot day pleasant.

The children's area is great. My 38' 3 year old can ride most of the rides, we have had very positive experiences with every staff member, and Boomerang bay also has a great area for little ones. The one serious problem I have encountered is charging $18 for a small locker at Boomerang Bay $23 for a large. Even if I had $18 extra dollars to spend no way would I pay for that! Very frustrated.

As I found out this past weekend, there is a right way and a wrong way to do Carowinds. This past Saturday for the second time on a weekend and I would recommend avoiding the weekends if you want to get on any rides.
 
The man and I are season pass holders so we normally go after work on nice days during the week and will work shifted hours so we have a half day in the middle of the week as a grown up "hookie day". These are the times to go! Especially if you go early in the season before the kiddos are out of school. 

We also opted for the meal plan so we have been scoping out all the dining establishments on site. Papa Luigi's is the best of the options for pizza and you can purchase overpriced alcohol here if you wish. Jukebox Diner has the best hamburger and a neat diner feel. Harmony Hall Marketplace has great AC, terrible hamburgers, okay pizza and BBQ but they do offer salad if you are looking for the healthy option. Every meal combo is $10.99 without a drink so keep that in mind when planning your day. They will give you a cup of water at every food station for free if you request it. 

I would avoid going during peak times if possible because then the majority of the day will be spent standing and waiting. The rides don't have wait estimations either so it is anyone's guess as to how long you will have to wait. When we were there last Saturday they were completely out of lockers too which meant we couldn't enjoy Boomerang Bang as much as we wanted. 

All said it is an okay place to go for locals but I would not drive out of my way to go. We live close so it works out for us.

If you have the option to go to any other park I would recommend that instead. I grew up going to Busch Gardens Williamsburg and have been to many parks along the east coast- this is the worst one I have ever been to. 

Carowinds has horrible line management. As you wait hours in line, you have to watch coasters go by with as many as ten empty seats. This may be due to the fact that you can't pick your seat, on most rides a worker is waiting to tell you where you can sit. One of our line waits was spent watching EMTs tend to a young man who had his face bashed open on the ride somehow. 

On top of that, my boyfriend and I encountered the rudest staff there. The second I walked in the gate, a teenager started yelling at me because I wasn't lifting my arms high enough for the security check- not a good way to start the day. While ordering lunch, there was a problem and the young girl sneered and rolled her eyes at us. When we spoke with the manager she told us point blank, "I'm not saying you're a liar but I don't believe you." Long story short we paid for an item they didn't have in stock and they wouldn't refund our money! They just expected us to pick something else- it was mind boggling. 

Overall the rides are mediocre and you won't get to ride many because of extensive lines (we made it to 5 in 10 hours). The majority of the rides are identical to those at Kings Dominion in Virginia , which we've always had positive experiences at. Avoid this place if you have the option.

The rides were pretty fun. The only
Other parks I've been to are six flags over ga and ca and I definitely don't think carowinds rides compare to theirs, but still a pretty good time. We were there from 10:45-3:45 and rose about 3 water slides, did the lazy river, sat and had an $8 beer, and rode about 4 coasters. So it wasn't too incredibly packed. Robert at dippin dots was extremely nice and helpful to us and we weren't even purchasing anything from him. He supervisor at "The Juke Box" where we purchased a beer was not very polite at all. His name was Jordan. Maybe he was just having a bad day, idk. As a matter of fact, everyone at he park was nice except for The juke box employees. Maybe Jordan's negativity trickles down. There was one girl, Tykia, who worked the register at the juke box and she was incredibly nice. Overall really good time, rides were fun but not too scary which is nice for some people, other people may want their rides a little more scary. Again, Robert at dip and dots and Tykia at the juke box, shout out to you both for going out of your way to make our visit pleasant!

Dinosaurs Alive is an additional $5.00 to get in, my 7 yr old loved it but the downfall is half the sensors didn't work until you were at the next dinosaur. The Fury 325 according to the kids was so scary they loved it I will not be reviewing it anymore because I'm not going on it LOL sorry. We had a great time Snoopy area was the only rides my son could ride he's 50" :/ the girls had a blast they loved the Nighthawk they loved the fact that they went upside down. we didn't hit the water park or water rides. They shut down the "high" rides about 9:30pm due to the weather. Lots of rides if you go after 4pm you will not have enough time for all the rides. it would take a couple of days to go on all the rides pick a cool day and spend the whole day there. the food is expensive we spent about $40.00 on a hamburger, salad, and chicken strips. No drinks we got souvenir cups (Free Refills) they had a country music show it was good. the chicken strips were dry, the fries were not done enough and the hamburger was falling apart. my husband bought a beer it was $8.71 I suggest you buy a souvenir cup and bring it back they are $0.99 refills during that season. I can't wait to go back.

I followed the construction of Fury 325 all winter and made it a point to visit this park because of that ride.  I was sad to find out that after I got there they really did not have much else that was different from other parks except for Intimidator.   I must admit that Intimidator was an amazing ride with a lot of out of your seat airtime and Fury 325 was so high and so fast that it was one of the best coasters I have ever been on.  Other than those two rides all else was old and had been there for many years.  The Carolina Cyclone and Thunder Road were the worst coasters I have ever been on, they were far to bumpy and whipped your head.  They should be closed down for good and removed from the park.  Hurler, Nighthawk and Afterburn were good rides just way to short.  Not much else was there, the flat rides left a lot to be desired.  I was very surprised and taken back by the lack of, almost non existent theming in this park.  Boomerang Bay water park was a poor excuse for a water park.  In this area as well there was not a bit of theming at all making it and eyesore to look at.  

We purchased parking and single meal tickets online before going to the park only to find out that you basically saved nothing at all.  Parking on Line was $15 and parking at the gate was exactly the same.  Here is the shocker, we paid $13.99 for a single meal plan online + tax and saved exactly .50 cents!  Really Cedar Fair?  .50 cents?  That is all the discount you could provide if purchased online?  What is really bad is the food was horrible!  The first day we had lunch at Harmony Hall and we had what they called "Steakburgers" which was the worst hamburger I have ever eaten.  The second day we had lunch in Boomerang Bay which was a grilled chicken sandwich with fries.  This was the driest Chicken sandwich I have ever had and to top it all off the condiments, Ketchup, mustard, mayo, bbq sauce etc was left out in pump containers in the blazing hot sun, it was disgusting.  Save yourself the cost of expensive park food and go across the street to Cracker Barrel and get a real meal for under $9.  

Purchased a tee shirt at one of the gift shops which was very reasonably priced at $12.99 + tax but the employees had not a clue.  Asked one employee if they had "package pick up" service and she said, "what is that" I explained and she told me to go ask guest services at the entrance.  Really, you don't know the answer to that simple question?  I asked another gift shop worker what the tax percentage was and he said and I quote "I don't know".  How in the heck would you not know the tax percentage and your working in a retail store? My rating for the tee shirt is 5 out of 5 stars because it was and excellent quality shirt for a good price. 

Overall we did have fun and it was worth the drive (10 hours) to ride Fury 325 and Intimidator but I will not go back to this park ever again and I would think twice before going back to a Cedar Fair property based on this park. 

The Busch Gardens family of parks are a better quality of park, better theming and better rides. I recommend you visit one of those parks.

Had an awesome time with my church family. The park was full of adventures. We got there early therefore it wasn't long waits for rides. We had 5 bus loads however the entry was very smooth. Most of the crew enjoyed the water park which was very packed but eventful.

Went on a Monday.  Weather was perfect. 
Customer Service: 3 stars- It really varied wildly.  Jessica was hands down the best ride attendant (5 stars for her).  I would say maybe 2 others from 10am- 10pm was at 4 stars and then the rest were dismal.  It was almost as if they were in a contest to see who could  ignore the kids the most and speak the least and mumble incoherently into the microphone.  The cleaning crews were terrible as well. Even if I pointed out a spill in a restaurant they would ignore it or go tell someone else to do it even if she/he was in the area anyway.  No one seemed to want to take responsibility.I will say that as far as directions go they were spot on and happy to help us find any place we wanted to get to.  And they were accurate.  5 stars for that!  I will do a separate food review for the park.
Hydration: 4 stars Online it clearly says $10.99 for a souvenir drink bottle but when you get there it's $14.99 unless you buy 3 or more. If you are a soda guzzler it's a good deal. If you go up to ANY food place they will give  you a tiny plastic cup of water for free because they are majorly short on water fountains.  This is a great service. We never were thirsty because it was a slow day and we did not have to wait in line as some of the places had a tray full of water ready for you.  Nice!  
Rides:4 stars  Hubby enjoyed the intense thrill of The Fury.  The line was only 45 minutes long so the kids and I watched a show while he rode it.  He gives it 5+ stars. Kids love all the rides in snoopy land.  Mama was bored with most of them but lines were short enough to ride their favorites twice.  I love the Peanuts characters that was a surprise bonus.  They even did a show at lunch in Harmony Hall.  
The show: 3 stars -It was a 60's tribute and I was surprised to see that they had the typical one black couple on stage and the rest were white kids sining glee style.  It was campy at best but my kids under 10 liked it enough to buy time for 45 minutes in an AC room.  The stage, seats, the building needs a major upgrade.  It still looked like it was from the 90s.  I was glad it was dark. I did not want to see how dirty it was. 
3 stars I was glad that the park had more mature trees finally.  I could find shade  here and there which was nice.  The grounds were really worn down though.  Everything really looked old and it's barely end of June.  Carowinds should invest in some sprucing up.  I will say that there were more trash bins in this place than I've ever seen anywhere.  Thumbs up for that.  And on our day they were properly emptied and never overflowing.  
Park layout: 4 stars.  it's simply a circle.  Nicely laid out.  Easy to get to everything.  Nothing was too far away from where you were.  One advantage of a small park.  You can do it in one day if you skip the water park like we did.  Some even managed to do both from what they told me in casual conversation. From 10:30 am - 10:00 PM we rode every ride we wanted including big coasters, did Planet Snoopy rides 100% and returned there at night to ride with lights.
Smoking: 1 star  WTF Carowinds?  it's 2015 and you are STILL allowing smoking?  REALLY?  There were smoking stations at the exits right where we got off rides so that you got a face full of smoke.  My kids were disgusted and I had to constantly move so I was not sitting near a smoker while I waited for my kids to exit.  Gross, unhealthy and gross! Allow vapes if you have to but say no to cigars and cigarettes please! And of course plenty of people smoked while walking around and in line regardless of the rules.  
Bathrooms: 4 stars
Plenty around - some very up to date others like the ones at state fairs just clean enough to deposit and leave.  They stayed clean most of the day which is short of amazing.  Harmony Hall had the cleanest bathrooms.  Yay. 
Park patrons:
No rating as that is out of Carowinds control.  But I will let you know that in Summer a lot of the local teenagers use it as their hangout.  It's a cheap season's pass for most of them and they park at a gas station or wendy's and walk over and take over certain sections.  They were so obnoxious in line at one of the Planet snoopy rides all in a big group singing loudly and clapping in your ears and being you know rowdy teens.   Lots of PDA and scantily clad teens and adults all over the park.  People are still littering which shocks me.  Smokers in line.  But I also met some super nice people who were having fun with their families and I was glad to meet them and chat.  Just know what to expect.

I have been trying to call customer service for the past week and have not been able to get anybody to answer. They have sold too many season passes, run too many specials and now the park is so busy, it is not enjoybale. My family has purchased season passes the last five years, this will be the last. I do not feel like the passes are of any value!

Review coming from a father of 1 girl and 4 year season pass holder...First, the good...season passes are the way to go if you live anywhere close.  After 2 times going it pays for it's self.  Plus, discounts on everything you buy except games if the pass is shown as well as free parking.  If you go a lot, purchase the souvenir cup.  It's pretty big and you can get free refills all season long of water at no charge and if you want soda it's something like $2.00 a refill...costs $15.00 but so worth it for the summer, just don't forget it.  In October there's Scarowinds.  Water Park called Boomerang Bay is not an additional cost and is attached to the park.  Quite large with a lot of choices for all ages in the water park. A ton of parking especially now that the South entrance is finally open.  Most of all, my daughter loves it and at age 7, doesn't even notice or care about the negatives that as an adult, frustrate me enough to loathe going to Carowinds
Now, the negatives...Boomerang Bay closes at 7:00pm...make is 9:00pm in summer months.  If you don't have season passes plan to spend a boat load of money.  Tickets are $50+ each, parking is $15.00 and food is ungodly expensive. Best bang for your buck is 2 slices of pizza and French fries for $12.00 over by the Superman ride, IMO.  Nothing is under $10.00 for any meal.  Carolina is HOT in the summer, be nice if they had a few mister tents around to walk through to cool off some.  The games are $3.00 a pop, did find one that was only $1.00 though.  The park was a nickelodeon theme park a few years ago and changed to The peanuts.  Kids now don't care or even know who Snoopy, Charlie Brown and the gang are, it was way better when it was Nickleodeon.  There is ONE exit line.  This may not seem like a big deal but at 9:30pm and park closes at 10:00, why is there ONE exit spot?

In a nutshell, it's not horrible for a large theme park but some little changes would make a huge difference...

If I could give this place ZERO stars I would. The customer service is atrocious. I understand weather is out of your control, but when you wait for 1.5 hours only to be told roller coasters are suspended due to weather and then are told it will be another 3 hours before they are back on...you'd expect some sort of return pass if you decide to leave. Instead, at Guest Relations an older lady named Lisa tells me, "we are open, and will be until 10pm." Ummm...excuse me!? How about you let me finish what I'm saying before you read from a prompt. How are you "open" if it's raining and roller coasters are out? I'm not one to argue, especially with someone that clearly doesn't get it. Stay away. If anything goes wrong you'll get the worst help ever.

Great place to visit when in NC and SC.  This park is located on the NC and SC border and goes back and forth across state lines.  The Fury 325 and Nighthawk are two of the best rollercoasters I have EVER ridden.  Also, we paid extra for the Fast Pass Plus.  If you can afford it, I highly recommend this pass.  It will substantially cut down on your wait times as you can bypass the extra long lines.  This pass allowed us to ride all of the roller coasters at the park in about 1/2 of a day.  Keep in mind that many of the roller coasters require riders to be taller.  I can't recall exactly how tall (I think 54") but I would double-check with the park before buying a fast pass that won't get properly utilized.  All in all, I would go back again if I lived closer. 

If you found this review helpful, please let me know.

Went to the waterpark yesterday and it was almost 100°.  There were not many cars in the parking lot and unfortunately we found out that the Southgate was not open. Now I understand that this does not include the food we buy and the drinks by when we are at the park. Coming from ohio, we are used to the best coasters on the planet at cedar point. These were very comparable. The fury war awesome. So was the intimidator and night hawk. We will definitely be back.

I live in Charlotte.  I  bought a season pass this year because in previous years i would go 2-3 times and spend more than what a pass cost.  

I think my purchase was a great investment.  I always have one weekday off so I can come when the park is dead...enjoy the water park during the heat...and ride rides at night after the water park closes.  It's a hell of a lot cheaper than a pool membership in town.  At times I have the entire park.to myself.

Parking is $15 bucks a pop.....so buying the season pass covers that every time....HUGE PLUS.

BE PREPARED.  FOOD IS EXPENSIVE.  I always bring a backpack with snacks and bottled water.  They never say anything at the gate.

It's great for people watching.  Lots of trashy people walking around in clothes too small for them.  You will see the occasional hottie too.

Oct is Scarowinds. ....

All in all, i will continue to come.  They are expanding the water park next year.  The  water park is already big

One of the best parks that I have had the pleasure to visit. The admission price was very reasonable for a 2 day pass. Souvenirs were well priced and the selection was large. Everything from t-shirts, beach towels, magnets and the list goes on and on. The food was kind of high for what it was but that is a commonality of most theme parks. Now for the rides... the coasters are plentiful and you will not be disappointed. There are also a nice selection of carnival type rides as well.  The employees were nice for the most part with an exception of when you ask for a glass of the free water that they announced numerous times over the loud speakers as perk on a hot day. Seemed as though it pissed off the teens working the drink concession stands. There is also a nice water park attached to the park that is included on the ticket price. This is a great park and you will not be disappointed!

Carowinds is an amusement park that sits on the boarder of North and South Carolina and attracts a huge amount of visitors every year. The park used to be owned by Paramount, but switched ownership several years ago. 

It seems like in the recent years, Carowinds has been revitalized to a certain extent. It was always a fun place to go with a few good rides, but it definitely needed a fresh coat of paint and some new attractions. Two of these newer attractions are the Intimidator and the Fury 325. I had a chance to try both of these during my last visit, and thoroughly enjoyed them! The Fury is the fastest Giga coaster in the world, reaching a peak speed of around 95 miles per hour. Thrill seekers will definitely be satisfied with this one!

With all of the cool attractions, there are a lot of things that can really make this park less attractive than it has the potential to be. First of all, the price of some of the food items is completely ridiculous. You should expect to pay more for things at an amusement park, but $16 for a few chicken nuggets, fries, and a medium soda is completely outrageous. The amusement games are also very expensive, like you would expect them to be at a fair. The staff that work here are mostly younger, and they seem to not be the least bit interested in being there to help you sometimes. Although most of them were nice, some of the workers running a basketball game were bouncing a ball around where I was eating and came close to bouncing a basketball into my food. You definitely don't want that, especially if you've just paid $16 dollars for your chicken nuggets.

Carowinds is a great place to take kids or go out on family outings, but I can't say that it is a place that you'll want to go all of the time. Although there are some downsides, Carowinds really does have SOME good staff and some really great attractions, and it is definitely worth a visit.

Apparently I'm still a kid at heart and more of an adrenalin junky than I remember. Visited the park for the 1st time in many years. Love the new entrance with the Fury 325 greeting you as you approach. Ok, let's get right to it. Fury 325....incredible, exhilarating, breathtaking and by far the best ride I've experienced here ever! I agree with some of the other reviews. This ride has a different experience depending on where you sit. Started off in the middle, then the back and on to the front. I have to say, the front seat was the best. We were here on a Thursday. One of the employee's said it's the slowest day of the week. Yes, we benefited from it. My daughter and I road Fury 8 times. I was sad that we missed the opportunity to ride Thunder Road one last time but it was old. Really enjoyed the Intimidator, Afterburn and Night Hawk(?). All the ride names have changed since my last visit. Oh well, still a blast. Has me contemplating getting a season pass for next year. Oh, one last note. The park gets pretty busy after 4pm. I guess there is discount tickets after 4.

These people are crooks. As soon as we parked, there was a rainstorm and they closed the rides. We could not get in until 8 (park closes at 10) and they would not discount the price. The worst thing was that, after taking our money, most of the rides were not running. I don't know whether it was the late time or the weather, but of course they did not mention that when they took our money. No way we would ever come back.

1. Visit: Went on a weekday with my family. Very hot day. Took some time off after lunch then continued.
It was summer holidays so bit crowded.

2. Parking: 15$ bit high. No problem in getting space during summer holidays.

3. Clean: Place is well maintained.

4. Fees: Got promotional deal of 35$ instead of 50+.
For that you can ride almost all rides and pool inside.

5. Rides: No brainer, Fury325 was our favourie. Lots of other good rides.
Though an old ride, Nighthawk I think, gave me back pain. If possible avoid it.

6. Pool: We didnt get to the water rides as it was getting late. For those of you near this place I suggest you get a season pass and visit it multiple times to cover entire place leisurely.

7. Staff: I don't know why others are complaining about staff. 
Staff were friendly and helpful. Not at all rude.

8. Food:
Thats the only negative of this place. Not at all value for money. Assume you gave it to a charity forcibly.

Final comment:
If you are within 200 miles from Charlotte I suggest you do visit this place atleast once.

A day at Carowinds makes for a good time. Carowinds may not be one of the most well known amusement parks, but it is certainly one of the better ones (especially within the Southeast). Since Cedar Fair acquired Carowinds, the park continuously gets updated and improved! Most recently, they built 2 GREAT coasters - The Intimidator and Fury 325. These 2 coasters are some of the best I have ever been on and I've visited most of the top 10 parks in the country! Carowinds does have a show that plays several times a day, but honestly, the only reason we go see it is to get a break from the heat. There is a great children's area, with Snoopy/Charlie Brown being the theme that consists of character meet & greets, dining, shopping, and rides. For NO EXTRA COST, you can visit Boomerang Bay, a fun water park, which they recently announced will be expanding. Improvements all around.

Except for certain sections, the park is smoke free (YAY!) and now they're beginning to sell alcohol, within certain areas. Food options have increased and improved with fresher foods and a wider variety of choices. (Expect to pay tourist prices everywhere within the park.) Parking is not free, but I don't know how much it costs because it's free with an annual membership, which I have. Looking for something fun to do in Charlotte? Go enjoy Carowinds!

Attention thrill-seekers, weekend warriors, and adventurers everywhere: if you're in the Southeast or are planning a trip through the region in the near future--do yourself a favor--plan on spending a day or two at Carowinds. Nestled right on the North and South Carolina junction near Charlotte, the amusement park is truly an underrated one. Most theme park enthusiasts have visited or at least heard of Six Flags, Cedar Point, Busch Gardens etc. Yet it seems that the "Thrill Capital of the Southeast" is still a little-known gem, despite forty-two years of continuous operation.

 Growing up in Columbia, SC (a short hour away), Carowinds was my childhood escape. Columbia being a sleepy little town, you couldn't help but feel stranded and bored in the summer time. While most kids counted down the days until summer break, I dreaded it--there's nothing glamorous about the blistering heatwaves and humidity that transformed the capital city into a desert mirage. Hence, I spent most days indoors, dreaming of waterparks and rollercoasters. After weeks of begging and pleading, my parents would give in and make my dreams come true; we'd pack into our jumbo-sized minivan and start our excursion to paradise.

 Even though every experience seems much more vivid and exciting to a child, I recently revisited my childhood muse with my younger brother and was delighted to see the theme park even more lustrous than I could remember. As we pulled into the parking lot, I could hardly contain my excitement seeing all the loopdeloops of new coasters we were anticipating. Having worked in the Hospitality Industry for several years, I've learned that presentation is everything; attention to detail and a polished appearance can make or break an experience. Carowinds has always had a wide variety of thrilling rides, but the shift in ownership from Paramount to Cedar Fair has given the property new life. From the fancy brick inlays and flag masts at the entrance to the state of the art Fury 325 giga coaster (tallest & fastest in the world) to the Boomerang Bay water park expansion project, the park has undoubtedly received a 21st Century facelift.

 As far as service is concerned, I have never had a bad experience in all my visits to Carowinds over the years. All the employees I have interacted with have been very professional, courteous, and eager to help. The workers on the rides and the lifeguards in the waterpark were particularly upbeat and very diligent with safety procedures. The park is clean and litter-free, and the upkeep of the public restrooms is exceptional. I am not a big fan of the food and refreshment prices, but no one ever said a trip to an amusement park would be a cheap affair. Even then, Carowinds offers membership in the form of season passes and runs the occasional promotion for cheaper entry.

 All in all, I went into my most recent trip to Carowinds with skepticism and lowered-expectations, yet ended up leaving the park with as big of a grin as the kids next to me. The park's growth is pretty consistent with Charlotte's sprawling urban metropolis, which is worth checking out while you're in the area.

This place was awesome! I went here for the first time last summer.  I then caught wind that they were building a new "giga-coaster"(more than 300 ft tall). This is the famed Fury 325 and it lives up to the hype. The first drop is literally like free-fall! In addition to the insane speed and the 150 ft tall "turn-around" element, it's actually RE-RIDIBLE!!!(you don't blackout).

The other pros for this park are Intimidator, Afterburn, and the drop tower. They recently built a new entrance which is pretty darn cool!

I live near DC and this park is about 400 miles from me.  I, however, will gladly pass up Kings Dominion and travel the extra distance to come here. That's how great of a time I had.

I'm VERY disappointed with the way Carowinds is run. I have been visiting this park for 15 years and when I went this past summer I was appalled! All the employees were EXTREMELY RUDE and seemed to HATE their jobs. One employee YELLED at me and my dad for nothing! It was so embarrassing! You CAN'T pick where you sit on coasters and when you ask for a certain row the employees very rudely deny your request. Also they won't allow loose articles on Fury which is totally fine, BUT they make you PAY for a locker! I bought a souvenir cup and then had to pay again to put it in a locker to ride Fury! Never have I had these problems at Carowinds until this year! They need to visit other parks and take a few pointers on guest service. Contemplating on whether I'll even go back again. The only reason I give 2 stars is because the coasters are great and I have great memories of visiting here when I was little. I even remember being able to pick where I sat on Intimidator. So sad Carowinds has become such a disappointment. Plus don't even try complaining to guest services. They could care less about your complaints and then tell you some bs excuse.

The rides are great and Scarowinds around Halloween is super  fun and unique. The day is ruined however when the park closes and it takes over an hour and a half to just leave the parking lot. It's unsafe and irresponsible of the park.

I have been planning a trip for my family based on the calendar provided by the Carowinds site. Today, Sunday October 18th, had been marked as the "Lowest Price" day. However when I went to buy tickets that are advertised at the lowest price of $53.99, the price in the cart jumped to $68.99 (same price hike for other admission types as well).

Well, I called the park and eventually got transferred to a manager at a "call center". The manager said that the price today was $63.99 and sort of just kept repeating that. I explained they are advertising a lower price on a day marked "Lowest Price" but she didn't budge. She then said that price being advertised is only for earlier in the year, but I countered that it's currently on the site being advertised -- if they had no plans of offering that price anymore, it should not continue to be advertised. 

She then placed blame on "the person who runs the website", and actually encouraged me to make a complaint against the web person. That's pretty dumb, the web person doesn't decide what's being advertised, they just follow orders from whoever runs ticketing. 

That person was fairly rude but this may of been because they didn't have authority to actually do anything. 

The advertised pricing is confusing to customers, and probably purposely so. It's a bait and switch with acknowledged intent to no longer offered a currently displayed price. The "As low as.." wording may have covered them if they didn't also have the "Lowest Price" designation clearly displayed on their calendar.

This is a frustrating and possibly illegal practice (admission confusion is a common problem at other parks too) and something hope Carowinds will change to better serve their customers.

Carowinds is amazing. My review is for the scarowinds. If you plan on going, spend the money on the fast lane or don't bother. It's only open from 7pm to 1am and you won't make it on more than 3 rides.

The new Carowinds.  This is 2015 and they have renovated the park, Fury has been unleashed and the staff, food, and experience in general is improved.  You still have lines to deal with but if you have a season pass and take advantage of Early Ride Times it is great.  One thing I have an issue with is there is no way, that I know of, to determine if the rides are running.  I have had guest come up and pay to enter only to find out once inside that a ride or rides are being serviced or affected by weather.  I understand these things happen, but you should disclose what is working and not working before taking someones money.  IMHO.  But I must say I like what they are doing with the park.

I told him that I called for tires cause I had a flat then, the guy said wait a minute and helped a guy who just wanted air in his tire so I waited for them to finish and he said how can I help you again and I said I would like a tire, then he asked for my keys said have. I been here before then said you can sit down now. If I wasn't form another city I wouldn't have come but I'm in a tight situation so I had to bite the bullet. Never again tho

I took my car here after my TPMS light came on. They found a nail in it, but also claimed my shocks were going bad 30,000 miles too soon.  However, it turned out my shocks were fine.  So these guys almost made me spend $250 for unnecessary repairs. Disgraceful.

If you already know what you need and are OK paying more for it here than any other place...  proceed.   They want to sell you anything regardless.

I asked to have one tire patched.   The manager was unable to give me any estimate for over 20 minutes until my car was on the rack and the wheel was off the car.   I asked three times how much patches cost.  He reluctantly said they average $30 eventually.   So mine will be less?   "Well, ummm...   no"

No shit, my tire is an above average achiever.  After the tire engineer inspected my tires his opinion was that it couldn't be fixed because it was too close to the sidewall.  I found this amazing given I could see it was over 1 inch from the sidewall into the treads.   The manager then pushed a full set of tires my way for $850.   He was surprised when I had them put it all back and I drove away.       

btw - The same set of tires at another shop was $700 out the door.   The other shop also patched my tire for $20 and laughed at this story.

In Oct. my son that is at  UNCC had a nail in his tire. The person at Tire Kingdom told him he needed 3 new tires., THe car is dented and has over 151,000 miles on it.We told him to match the tread. Instead of giving him options of prices they put on$ 184.00 tires EAC on the vehicle. I called very upset the next morning and the manger said he would not give me an exchange nor would he give me any money off. He offered a 4th tire with a $70.00 rebate and would discount an oil change! This is taking advantage of a young consumer and  in my opinion a terrible way of doing business. I would NEVER recommend this company.

The new service manager Kenny was extremely polite and helpful in explaining options for my wife's vehicle. I've been coming to this location for over a decade and have always been pleased with the services received.

Sorry to be so late writing.. I went there on 7/10/2014 for an oil change.I had my rear brakes repaired at my dealership & went to TK for the oil change since I had bought tires there I get free rotation. They told me I needed front brakes. They had my car on the lift and told me to 'feel' the steel part of the wheel (as though I would know anything?). I mentioned my car riding rough (could feel the bumps in the road). They proceeded to tell me I needed struts as well. They showed me torn bellows (I googled the name) and acted as though that was serious. I only paid for the oil change then promptly called my dealership & they told me to come there. They also said the struts are fine, and the bellows are simply dust catchers. During my oil change at TK, I left with an estimate of $730.35! for nothing I needed! I filed a complaint with corporate.
