Moderately spiced and served over Rice."  They give you the option of splitting it for only $5.00 more bringing the entree price to 23.95.  Certainly not cheap by any means, but well worth the cost.  The best way to describe the taste, is to image garlic, butter, onions, and a bunch of "Queens Magic Spices" working harmoniously to perfectly marinate the shrimp with the rice keeping things from getting to sloppy.  Its Cajun food at its finest.  

At that point, things were so good we just HAD to get dessert, right??  We decided to order the pecan pie.  I mean, pick an adjective - amazing, spectacular, splendid, etc.  It was served to us warm and moist (that's what HE said - LOL), as if it was just taken out of the oven, with dab of whipped cream.

The service was on point from start to finish; from the valet to the host/hostess to the super friendly bartender upstairs.  Everyone was really kind and polite. What exactly separates the staff here from other restaurants?  Its all in the details...for example, every single person said, "be with you in one minute" or "be right with you".  No one ever ignored us, or expected us to wait until we could be helped.  My drinks (adult/H2O) were never empty. We didn't have to think/worry about parking.  There was a plethora of condiments, hot sauces, etc to satisfy even the most particular taste buds.  Bathrooms were immaculate.  They had live jazz.  ...See what I mean about the details?

I'm hooked.  I'll be back very, very soon, maybe even tomorrow!  I love this place.  There.  I said it!

First Saturday night of restaurant week was a zoo, but our server Alex did a great job and was even accommodating to our most demanding guest and made her smile and happy. Restaurant week menu items were of a good cross section of picks as we tried most of them and we're quite pleased.

I'd had this place bookmarked to try for a lonnnng time! So when my friends suggested it for Restaurant Week I was obviously elated. Finally!!! 

And they did not let me down!!! It met all of my expectations and more. 

I like that their menu for Restaurant Week includes all of their classic dishes and a glass of wine! 

I decided to go with the seafood gumbo, étouffée with all three (chicken, shrimp and crawfish) and the key lime our for dessert. 

The seafood gumbo was classic. It was warm and hearty with just the right amount of spices. The étouffée was nothing short of amazing!!! I'm basically a fan of this dish for two reasons....one they are not skimpy with any of the meat selections and two it's sooo spicy! I definitely recommend sopping....(yes sopping) up some of that delicious sauce with those rolls. Yum. 

Not to be outdone the key lime pie was a great way to end the meal. 

Add to an amazing meal a live band and complimentary valet....this place is definitely worth a visit!

We had to visit Charlotte's best cajun joint before we headed home to NYC. 4 stars for the haunted black magic atmosphere of the restaurant. Even in broad daylight, the dining hall had a dark shrouded vibe going on. The beignets let me down a little bit but the shrimp & grits more than made up for it. The fried popcorn shrimp was also very well done but the highlight for me was the shrimp & grits.

This place is great. It looks small on the outside but it's gigantic on the inside. Very quaint and reminiscent of an abode in the French quarter. I had the popcorn crawfish and the red beans and rice here. Both dishes were awesome. The pop corn crawfish was meaty and had a slight hint of spice to it not salty or anything. Let's not talk about the sweet tea. That was just marvelous. Not too sweet. It was just right.

Cajun Queen serves up consistent cajun food in a fun environment.  It's not exactly what you would find dining out in NOLA, and it's a bit pricey for what you get, but if you have a craving, it will fix that.

The one thing that makes Cajun Queen stand out is the rooftop dining.  It's a great place on a nice night.  There is also live jazz in the upstairs dining section.  

Word of warning - if you order a cocktail, you only need one.  ;)
Wonderful Cajun cuisine, great live jazz music, and fantastic wine selections. Such a treat for date night!

I went to cajun queen with some friends from work a while back. I had the Diane, which people seem to be raving about on yelp. It was okay. I found the favors to be very mild and uninteresting; there was no spicier or complexity to the meal. The live music was nice but makes me wonder if this place would be appropriate for a quiet, romantic dinner. I will probably give cajun queen another try just in case it was an off night.

We didn't try the food because we just wanted some wine, but it all smelled amazing and when we arrived at 4:30 we were asked if we had a reservation so I'm thinking they're usually pretty booked up! 

Service was good in the bar...definitely enjoyed our wine and the atmosphere. Great way to get that Southern feel! At 6pm their live jazz started up. I was hoping for some more lively music, but it was more easy listening which was understandable given the size of the restaurant and the close proximity of the band to diners.
This is hands down my favorite restaurant in Charlotte. I've tried almost everything and have never once been disappointed. Great staff and even better environment. Nothing beats Cajun Queen!!

So about 10 years ago I was taken to Cajun Queen by some friends when I moved here to Charlotte from Chicago. Remembering that I was not crazy about it, I still was open to going again to re try it. I searched through all the Yelp reviews to see what to order and what was the best. 
First...this old House or Restaurant should be updated..obviously with the amount of people in it  at the time I left...they have the money. Stair case is wiggley..and it is just plain old..Not quaint and old ..just old.
We were a big party and we had a good server named IVY, but the food left lots to be desired. We were kindly treated by our hosts to almost ever single one of the appetizers to begin with. This started with Fried Oysters that were for sure fried a couple of days ago and then reheated in a microwave! ..Fried Green tomatoes were straight out of frozen bag and not fried..just barely baked..still cold in the middle..very bland. The New Orleans style Barbequed Shrimp....tiny little salad size and in the same sauce that everything including the gumbo had. 
I am going to spare you anymore..but to tell you It will for sure be another 10 years before I go back...thank goodness the company was fantastic!!

Do not waste your money! The gumbo tasted like the roux had burned and there was no salt whatsoever. I ordered the blackened chicken to be safe thinking "no one can mess up blackened chicken".....I was wrong. None of the food (including the blackened chicken) were seasoned with salt and pepper. This was the most bland, overpriced food I'd ever had in the city. I ordered my toddler the chicken strip little gators meal. The fries were the best thing out of the entire meal. The service was as also dry and not very friendly or inviting from the hostess to the waiter, Brandon. Geez, I know it's a Tuesday night (we arrived at 5:30) but at least show some enthusiasm as I arrive to spend a whopping $123 (4 entrees, 4 alcoholic bevs, 1 kids meal) on a below average meal. It would've been more had we been charged for the uneaten cup of gumbo.
Have been there a few times and they never disappoint!  The Jambalaya is second to none.  Perfectly spiced and portioned.  The New Orleans BBQ is also excellent.  Great atmosphere and service.

The fried oysters are to die for.

The crayfish scampi looks great but a bit too garlicky.

The BBQ shrimp is just a-ok.

Real cool how they turned an old house into CQ.
Excellent food the price is comparable especially on the creole dishes. You have to make reservations if you want to get a good seat otherwise come before six o'clock.

I'd probably give 3 1/2 if I could but I'm going to give 4 stars for excellent service... love the live music every night, great drinks, outdoor patio.  I like the old house. It feels like going over an old family members house but better. 
The food was good overall.  Appetizers Bbq shrimp sauce is great with bread and the Crawfish ceviche was flavorful and spicy!  So when my gumbo came it tasted blah to me. Not very flavorful.  So my dad ate it and liked it. My shrimp and grits were ok but the shrimp was bland and the skin on my sausage was hard. My sister had the dish several times before and said it didn't taste the same. Liked the grits though. tasted the blackened catfish... moist and delicious. Tasty desserts, but nothing to write home about. I do think it's a bit overpriced. 

The restroom paper towel machine was broken. And no other dryer or towels available. I know is out of their control but maybe need a backup.  It's quite annoying.

Great place for appetizers, live jazz and drinks.

This is one of the few spots in Charlotte that I constantly find myself going back to. I like trying different things at restaurants, but every time I go in I can't help but get the Crawfish Scampi to start off and the Chicken Diane as an entree. The flavors and seasoning are unbelievable and the atmosphere is great upstairs with a Jazz band playing every night.

Although I have passed this location on many trips to  Charlotte as well as when I lived her, today is my first time sampling the cuisine. I started with a very delicious key line Martini and the popcorn  crawfish both a sweet treat. The crawfish for sure should not be missed. Next course was a very fresh and impeccably spice cup of gumbo. For my main course I chose from the specials menu a piece of Mahi Mahi topped with shrimp taoso ham roasted red peppers and mushrooms served over garlic mashed potatoes.  The presentation was beautiful and the taste divine. All if the seafood was extremely fresh.   My husband chose this Resturant to celebrate our Anniversary and I am very pleased with his choice.

Food was tasty but the seating could be more comfortable to a point of wanting to hang out for a bit to listen to music and have some drinks. Wait staff are very nice a knowledgable about the menu. Highly recommend the "Shrimp and Crawfish" app to start and "7th St. Stumbler" as you drink. Do the complimentary valet parking sons not to have parking issues.

I have been in Charlotte for over three years and had never been to Cajun Queen, but I have been listening to Jazz a lot lately and got in the mood for some live Jazz. From what I have been able to find, this is the only place in Charlotte that even has live Jazz, so I booked a reservation (through OpenTable) for my girlfriend and I on a Saturday night.

No problems with the reservation or getting us seated as soon as we got there, but I was immediately disappointed to find out that the music was only upstairs and there would be a "20-30 minute wait" for seating upstairs. We were seated downstairs, right next to the entrance--it's not great seeing everyone come and go, as well as the staff milling about the hostess stand.

Our dinner started with no live Jazz (from downstairs it sounded like pots/pans being banged together) and less than ideal seating. Then came the food. It wasn't awful, but it wasn't anything special. Certainly not good enough to warrant all of the rave reviews here or the prices they charge. It was seasoned, but still tasted very bland to me, especially the crawfish, which I thought was overcooked. The seasoning certainly did not taste Cajun to me. (I got the crawfish Creole and my girlfriend had the chicken Etouffee.)

I was definitely not pleased with my first--and last--experience at Cajun Queen, and left $60 poorer and hungry for better food, although I was full. Given that "Live Jazz 7 nights a week" is prominently touted on their website header, they really need to specify that it is only upstairs. I would have requested upstairs seating when I made the reservation, if I had known that was the only place to hear the music. Either that, or they need to remodel that old, bland house to open it up more.

Bottom line: I will not be going back.

Having been to NOLA and experiencing the amazing food scene it's hard to imagine anywhere outside of LA being able to match the quality of food; however, this restaurant is awesome.  The etouffe was spot on, shrimp and grits creamy, the Cajun popcorn was a delightful surprise and the scampi unlike any other ever tried. 

Great place to celebrate or just enjoy a great taste of new Orleans.

One of our favorite restaurants in Charlotte.  Food is excellent.  Sometimes it gets a bit loud inside when dining (reason for 4 stars not 5), so we ask for outside patio seating, weather permitting.  Service always good, food always excellent.  I have dined there dozens of times and never had a bad meal.  Highly recommend.

When I found out we were going here for brunch while I was in town, I was excited.  I had not had beignets since I was in Nola in April and I was craving them.  When we arrived at 10 to 11 (brunch begins at 11), there was already a line of people waiting outside.  The doors opened and people walked in like they had not ate in years, we knew we were in for a treat.  The restaurant is within what appears to be a house.  The dining rooms are where a living room and a den would typically be.  We were seated by the fireplace, which was running since it was 45 degrees outside.  The decor is very quaint and welcoming, almost like you're visiting a relative's house.

The dinner menu is also available all day but you truly go to this place for brunch.  I originally asked for a coffee with amaretto but they don't serve alcohol before noon (I'm spoiled from NY brunches) but their regular coffee was just as good.  We started off with an order of beignets.  6 perfectly sized fried balls of dough were presented with the most delicious strawberry compote in the middle for dipping.  The beignets were perfect and light and that compote made my day.  

For our entrees, we each got something different and decided to pick and choose from the other plates.  I got the bacon, egg, and cheese omelet.  This omelet was thick with a whole layer of bacon going through the center.  It also came with a side of cheesy grits, which were also delicious, and fresh fruit.  My friend got the bananas foster French toast.  The bananas were sweet but good and the toast itself was fluffy and delicious.  My other friend got the rice and beans, which yes becomes an entire meal since sausage is also included.  These were some of the best rice and beans the three of us have ever tasted.  And this is coming from a Puerto Rican, who also confirmed their tastiness.

Overall, this is a fantastic place for brunch.  Get there early, and try a little bit of everything.

I take everyone that comes to visit me to Cajun Queen!  From the great food (my favorite is the bbq shrimp and bread to dip into the sauce), to the live jazz and great service, this is a restaurant not to be missed!

I've been to Cajun Queen a few times now and I've been extremely satisfied with both the high level of customer service and also the food quality.  First, I showed up about 20 minutes late for my reservation (I know, I'm that guy) and they were able to seat us right away on a Friday night.  No questions, no hassle, they simply sent us to an open table as if we had showed up right on time for our reservation.  We had our 3 year old son with us so we each breathed a sigh of relief once seated.

Initially I wasn't sure what to order, until I started leafing through pictures on Yelp.  While it all looked good, the Shrimp and Grits stopped me in my tracks.  It wasn't your everyday Shrimp and Grits as they've given it a nice Cajun twist by adding a tasty creole sauce.  The shrimp had a distinct smokey flavor that worked really well with the dish.  The Andouille sausage also packed a nice punch that really pulled the whole meal together.  

For dessert we ordered the Tollhouse Cookie Pie.  I had never had anything quite like it before.  It was really good; however, we both felt as though it could have had more chocolate chips.  The walnuts added a nice dimension too.
Just go.  Great service and good food!
Great atmosphere, Great food. The waiter Alex is the best at what he does. Truly had a great time!!!
Food is always good and very consistent.  Coming here for years. Heres a few pics of our dinner: Chicken Diane, Shrimp scampi, fried green tomatoes.

Very enjoyable dining experience.  The service was friendly and timing was good.  Food was very good quality and taste.  Serving quantities was adequate.  Nice menu selections and drink offerings.  Highly recommend dining here.

All around this place was great! Atmosphere is one of a kind and when they had the band upstairs, it's a different feel. The food was very good and plenty. Staff was very friendly and informative. Very close to where we live and we will definitely be back.
wonderful food and wonderful music every night

We had heard a lot about this place and decided to dine in here during the Charlotte Restaurant Week. We have been to this place only once so far. Just to be safe we made reservations. I will say this place has a beautiful ambiance. It looks like a house which is converted to a beautiful restaurant. There is valet parking available. The receptionist at the front gave us a nice seat on the second floor. It was just our luck because there was live jazz music being played that night. During the restaurant week, this place does have a very good choice of Entrees. You will be served with a 3 course meal with the addition of a glass wine of your choice. We had the cup of seafood gumbo to begin with. The soup served was the right quantity. Not too much or too less. Soup was warm enough. The contained scallops, shrimp, vegetables. For the entree, we had Diane with Chicken and Fresh Fish (blackened Tilapia). Both the chicken as well as fish we cooked well. The topping on the fresh fish were great. The diane chicken had a variety of vegetables on it along with rice. You can also have shrimp and chicken together in it. The food was warm. The third and final course is a dessert of your choice. We chose to have the Key Lime Pie. I cant remember much but I don't think a Key Lime Pie can go wrong at all. The server was definitely very polite and nice to us. She was checking on us at regular intervals and the food was served in a timely manner. During restaurant week, I would say the price of the meal is $$. However if you decided to go some other time, then it would be $$$. The restrooms were clean and tidy.
Food is always great and service is good! Best brunch in Charlotte. My son loves the beignets and they sell out quick...

DISABLED PEOPLE, PLEASE BEWARE

 I've been a patron of Cajun Queen for over a decade but my experience tonight was humiliating. I treated my sister to  a birthday dinner and despite our online reservation, we were asked to leave in  the most demeaning of ways. I have a debilitating childhood disease and use a wheelchair on occasion ; tonight was one such occasion. I could only order food I knew didn't require cutting, so I opted for potatoes and a salad. My sister ordered a full meal with wine. I had two mixed drinks (so we're not cheap diners). We had to signal for another glass of wine for my sister, despite seeing the party next to us being served appropriately. 

I'm not sure why we were overlooked but I'm left to wonder if it's the small portion I ordered that was disparaging.

Anyway, when my sister went to look upstairs a minute to reminisce, our server asked my sister quite off the cuff, "Do you want help with 'her' (wheel)chair? I kinda need that table."

Taken aback, my sister said, "No." 

We took note of the EMPTY tables on BOTH sides of us and the fact that the restaurant wasn't crazy busy as we remembered. 

I spent $67 on a tab for two  and left a TIP of $20--clearly more than twenty percent.

I don't know many people who tip as graciously as I  do. My reasoning for leaving the tip despite the service, was it being Christmas time and it's something I do for goodwill.

When we rolled to the handicap ramp, it was completely (I mean, completely) blocked off by an A-frame sign about parking; see for yourself. Had  my sister not been with me, I would have not been able to access the restaurant at all.

I haven't  always been disabled and ran a restaurant, myself (loved every minute of it). I know how people can take advantage (campers) and I know people can be uber-cheap at tipping. I don't fall into  either ilk. I know good service when I see it; I know how to approach diners who overstay their 'welcome (their can NEVER be anyone who overstay their welcome; consider it flattery); it's part of doing business and keeping patrons happy.  Take a loss here and there. 

We were in and HOME in a little over two hours. The couple beside us with the adorable little girl who  laid all over the booth was fine by me; she's a child and CQ is a noisy place. 

I felt a sting of angst when I asked for my food to be wrapped. The facial gestures were quite unsettling.

Please don't tell me I'm sensitive: I've had over FORTY surgeries--TWO with NO painkillers afterwards. I've walked on a BROKEN leg to buy wrapping paper tape been accosted because I wasn't 'messed up' "enough'" to ''deserve a handicap tag. 

So enough ---but there's  no excuse for inhospitably between diner and those needing  to use the facilities.''PLeASe let these be a isolated parents.'

PLEASE LEAVE :)

Two recommendations.  1. Get the Duck.  2. Order one of the fish specials and pick your toppings.  Oh wait three recommendations---eat it upstairs with the Gator Band.  The guys are as funny as they are old.

Warning:  By far the best dish on the menu is the BBQ shrimp.  My mouth is watering just typing the name (no kidding).  But it will give you some "special" breath.  Bring mints.

Tip: The Étouffée, Diane and Creole travel well and are good for catering.  We actually had a sampling for our Christmas party years back. Yum.

If you can handle the calories the BANANA FOSTERS french toast is crazy good.  I mean crazy crazy good.  It's a good thing I think they only do breakfast once a week.

My husband and I went for dinner and ate upstairs, enjoying the bar area first.  We popped outside with our drinks and ran into members of the house band. Had a wonderful time talking to the musicians.  The food was delicious, and the menu has  gluten free options too.   If  you want to enjoy the jazz, reserve a table upstairs, preferably when there isn't a wedding party. Really loved the music!

We have been to the Cajun Queen many times and have always had a fantastic meal.  Our favorites are the fried oysters and the Wash Day Blues. It's our favorite restaurant, even though it's a long way from Weddington.  Well worth the drive, and we will continue to dine here as often as we can!

I take everyone that comes to visit me to Cajun Queen!  From the great food (my favorite is the bbq shrimp and bread to dip into the sauce), to the live jazz and great service, this is a restaurant not to be missed!

We went there, for the hundredth time, but this time armed with a Groupon. The process was seamless since hey now scan the coupon at the table with their handheld device.  

The food was great!  I had shrimp and grits!  Halfway through my meal, a bug flew into my food from the light over head.  The waiter quickly removed my plate, comped my meal, and gave me a fresh plate.  I was very impressed.  

I would def go back!  Their waitstaff have certainly improved their skills with dish removal during the meal. And, they are very friendly and professional.  

Great job!

Very loud, bad service, and the food doesn't met the expectations. We came w a party of 10 people, we didn't even get menus for a while, it was so loud we could hardly listen to our server. Dirty plates were sitting in our table for a long time. Super disappointed

It has an amazing atmosphere and very unique. Our server was very polite and was on top of everything, even the hostess was great she found us seats upstairs near the live music and the food was everything I expected and more. It makes you feel like New Orleans in Charlotte...we're already planning our next dinner here, I definitely recommend the restaurant as a must visit

The owner could care less about customers. He is the rudest man. The food is so so. Nothing Cajun about it. They did not use our Groupon correctly. That was fine with us, but why couldn't the server tell us. Not just toss the bill on the table and walk away. Save your money and dine elsewhere. The Cajun Yard Dog is far better, and far more Cajun cuisine.

We love the Queen and once again we were not disappointed. Outstanding all the way around. One of the best ambiance restaurants I have ever been in. Highly recommend the crawfish scampi appetizer and blackened or fried catfish. Their complimentary valet parking is the icing on the cake. Great place!

This place is great!  The atmosphere is like a southern home in Louisiana.  The food was delicious; however, I give it four stars because our waiter wasn't the best.  I went with 2 of my friends (we're all under 30) and they didn't serve us the way he served the people beside us.

We first ordered the gumbo, which wasn't bad.  It wasn't as tasteful that I thought it would be.  However, using our bread with the gumbo, made it so much better.  The bread soaked up the gumbo and gave it a little bit of a buttery taste.

As for my entree, I ordered the etouffee four ways.  On the menu, it list three ways, but u can get four ways (which includes andouille sausage).  My friend ordered the shrimp etouffee. 

As close friends do, we tasted the other and we both found mine to be better because the andouille sausage gave it a little bit of a sweeter taste that mixes well with the spices.

I'd recommend this place!

FYI:  There's sometimes groupons that make it a cheap place to eat! Keep a look out!

This was my favorite restaurant in Charlotte 20 years ago.  Many new restaurants have come to town since then...and this is still my favorite.  The food is authentic, the ingredients are fresh and high-quality, the service is friendly, and the atmosphere is great.

Came with a friend and the house is really cute. It's a plus that they also have valet parking when you pull up. Inside is nice. Atmosphere is warm and cozy. We sat by the fireplace. I ordered the etouffee with chicken, shrimp and crawfish. It was good. Very flavorful, I didn't even have to put tobacco sauce in it because the spices were on point. I wasn't crazy about their bread, it was really hard. My friend had the gumbo soup and I tried it and it was delicious. They were pretty busy on a weekday. We saw the waiter maybe 3 times-When he greeted us, when he took our order and dropped off the check. He never came by in between to check on us or fill up our drinks.Service wasn't that great but I will definitely give it another try. Other than that, food was good!

5 hours ago 

Had reservations for 5:30. Arrived on time and were greeted by 2 hostesses promptly. Very pleased. Myself, coworker and my sister. Here for restaurant week, we were promptly seated. 5 stars. Server was prompt & attentive. We ordered our wine and 1st course same time. Arrived in 5 to 8 mins. 5 stars. Ordered entrees & dessert when 1st course arrived. No problem, smooth execution. Entrees arrived soon after finishing 1st course. We all ordered the Diane, sister w/chicken, coworker and I, three ways. All were delicious! Dessert was brought to our table boxed for takeout, which we requested. All in all excellent service. No complaints.

I'm not sure why this place is rated 4 stars. The food is barely ok. The shrimp are actually tiny frozen shrimp..not fresh or local. The gumbo taste watered down and the service sucks to the 10th degree! We waited all of 15 min before our waitress finally said, "I'll be right with you".  She came back 10 min later. I attempted to order the pasta on the menu for restaurant week, but was I was informed that option is not available until 4 pm because it's a dinner option. Wth? Why is it on the menu? We were seated in the back which was full. And also full of spider webs and uncleanliness. Don't waste your time. Go to a better Cajun restaurant, this one is not worth your money.

Let me just say the only reason I am giving this place 2 stars is because my boyfriend liked it. We went here as our second restaurant for restaurant week. The wine (cabernet) was decent enough. For the appetizer we ordered the gumbo and the caesar salad. I can't rate the gumbo because I'm not a fan of what's in it. I was told it was good though. The salad was just a salad nothing great. For the main course we ordered the chicken etouffee and the cajun chicken pasta. The chicken in the etouffe was the same texture and taste as you'd get from takeout chinese food which my boyfriend said that's why he liked it. The sauce was okay but it didn't save the dish. The cajun chicken pasta was ehhh. It was eatable but again I'd never go back for it. Dessert consisted of bread pudding and key lime pie. The boyfriend liked his bread pudding but I wasn't a fan and my key lime pie was good but I would swear it was Sarah Lee!! I feel no need to ever come back to Cajun Queen, the food just wasn't great and really a spice let down considering it's supposed to be cajun and it's not a very comfortable restaurant.

I have been to Cajun Queen Twice and have enjoyed my meal both times. The portions are enough for two to share. I ordered the fried catfish last night and got two big pieces of fish which was way more than I expected. It was well seasoned with a lightly fried coating which didn't flake. My husband order a dish (Diane something) which consisted of crawfish, shrimp, and chicken) which was amazing. We both had plenty of leftovers to go. Our server Justin was on point and very attentive. I usually don't remember names but he was awesome. I love the quaintness of this place. The Groupon deal is awesome. Not sure how long they plan on running this deal but I would go back despite the deal.
Good cajun restaurant in Charlotte.  The fried oysters are out of this world!

My husband and I went here for dinner on a Thursday night. Atmosphere was nice. Nice and cozy.  Although, It was very dark, so dark that I had to use the flashlight on my phone to see the menu. The band was a disappointment. Pretty dull much older gentleman playing. The fried green tomatoes were delicious. The fried catfish and the red beans and rice were bland and lacked seasoning. My husband had the blackened catfish which was very good. Service was excellent. Overall it was just an ok experience. We probably wouldn't go back

This place is pretty good. It's more of an upscale cajun joint. If you are looking for fancy cajun - this is your place. I prefer a good dive (there was one down the street from this place - Bayou Kitchen - it deserves honorable mention - it was a better example of real cajun food). The food is good - the location - also nice. I took one star away because it's not as good as the place that was just down the street.

I only hear great reviews for this restaurant. So I knew it was time to go when I saw there was a Groupon. They offer free valet which makes it a lot easier since I had no clue where to park and they will tow your car if you  park else where. The manager immediately opens the door for us as we approach and we got seated right away. We did make reservations in advance though. I was shocked to see a live band playing on a Wednesday night but apparently they are there 7 days a week! I enjoyed the live music and fireplace that adds on the ambiance. Our server was okay, he gave us bread and provided enough time for us to look through our menu. We decided to go with the Etouffee and Diane. Both had chicken, shrimp and crawfish. I liked the Etouffee but man... I miss the Diane already. I've been starring hard at the Cajun Queen groupon again because I'm already carving for another dish. My boyfriend just recently told me they are $4 cheaper if you get the voucher on living social. You won't be disappointed if you're looking for a new restaurant to try in Charlotte. We can't wait to come back.
need to check out pricing
Great atmosphere in and old converted home. The food is great too!

Cajun Queen wasn't awful, but it wasn't great either. If you've been to New Orleans and sampled the fare, then you will be disappointed with the cuisine. While not on par with New Orleans, it's not without charm. Still, not the Big Easy. 

For scale: 1- ingesting Old Bay seasoning, 
2 - a box of Zatarain's, 4 - Cajun Queen, 
10 - New Orleans.

The service was great, but we could tell our waitress was overworked even with the servers assistants refilling waters and removing finished plates. 

Everything arrived lukewarm; gumbo, the "all 3" (crawfish, shrimp, and chicken) étouffée, and even the broccoli side. And although the étouffée cautioned, "Spicy!," it was tame. 

One winning aspect was the Sazerac cocktail, and New Orleans beer on the menu (Abita). 

We'd go again for drinks.

I've been to New Orleans many times and have experienced some great Cajun style food, so I have pretty high standards.  For the most part, from what I've ordered, CQ does a decent job.  I've been twice and ordered the Étouffée both times because it's very good.  It's got the perfect amount of spice that pairs well with an ice cold Abita.  The BBQ shrimp is a great app as well.  It's not so much about the shrimp as it is the sauce you dip the bread in.  Delicious.  My girlfriend was hit and miss with her entrees in the 2 times we've been.  The shrimp Diane was just OK.  It's a lighter consistency than the Étouffée and doesn't have the kick I look for when I'm in the mood for Cajun.  The shrimp and grits weren't good at all.  The grits were bland and the blackened shrimp didn't hit the mark.

Overall, I enjoy coming here, but the prices are a little high in my opinion.  They have a Groupon & Living Social pretty much all the time, so don't forget to grab one before you go!

Crawfish is always good. They open at 11am on Sunday for brunch. Price Avg $10-13. The only thing I don't like about Cajun Queen is their tables are too close to each other but they always have a full house that explain why they need so many tables. I hope they will move to a bigger place in the future.

This was my first time trying this particular restaurant.  I've visited New Orleans quite a few times, and was excited to get the opportunity to go there.  The atmosphere had a very intimate setting. However, I was looking forward to their catfish.  When the waiter stated that they ran out 10 minutes before we got there, we had to pay for an uncharge for a better fish.  Didn't quite understand that, since they were the ones that ran out of the catfish.  I'll go back there, but not anytime soon.

Seated promptly at 5:30 right by the fireplace.  Staff friendly and helpful. Ordered fried green tomatoes. Good and the sauce on top tasty still like the ones from Tupelo Honey better. Next time will definitely try the bbq shrimp. I ordered the shrimp creole and salad my husband had the Cajun pasta and cup of gumbo.  Everything was great especially the Cajun pasta.  Next time I would skip the salad if ordering an appetizer because portions are very generous and the shrimp creole was full of shrimp. Only negative is parking. Which is pretty much non existent so make your reservations early.
Great food nice atmosphere, service was great. There was a mix up with our food, manager came without requesting and comp our meal. Will definately return!

We eat at the Cajun Queen regularly...there are always Groupons!  My dad is from Louisiana so he knows his cajun/creole food, and this place has fantastic food.  Amazing atmosphere!!  One of my favorite restaurants ever.

We had a great experience at this restaurant. Its a unique atmosphere being in a old house. The place was packed the night we went. You definitely need a reservation here on the weekend. We arrived a few minutes early, and were directed upstairs to the bar area. This area was packed and there was a small band playing blues/jazz. It was a great vibe, great atmosphere. I hated to leave there, when our table was ready. But alas, we were called away to a downstairs table. Downstairs, I could no longer hear the band. However, we ordered the special for the night. They had several different kinds of fish, with several different cajun toppings. The food was plentiful and fantastic. This place just has a lot of character and thus it makes a great place for a date night. I probably wouldn't bring the kids here, because they wouldn't appreciate it. But a great place for a nice couples night out, or a dinner date with friends.

The crawfish scampi and Tilipia with crawfish topping was awesome as always, extremely consistent, exception being the gumbo, it is not typical Louisiana roux based gumbo, I will not order again. I also only give 4 stars, as Brandon, our Server, must have had something or someone else on his mind as he barely had us on his mind. Next time we will ask for Samantha, or Sam, best server in the house.
Got the crawfish ettuofe.  It was the best Cajun food I have ever had. Absolutely fantastic. Spicy and extremely flavorful. A must go for any traveler.

The food was incredible, I got blackened catfish and my fiance got Diane with chicken, shrimp and crawfish and a side of andouille sausage and everything was great. The "steamed" broccoli on my plate was more dipped in hot water and still raw but it still tasted great. We also both got desserts, the key lime pie (my all time favorite dessert) and that was incredible and the bourbon pecan pie, which my fiance said was also amazing and was served warm. The reason for 3 stars is the service. Our waiter, Brandon, acted like he couldn't care less that we were there, just kinda threw the food down and walked away, checked on us only once and honestly just didn't even try to offer good service. The bus boy who refilled water, brought bread and took our plates came around more often than he did. However, when a group of older people came in he was so attentive and pointed out everything on the menu to them, went over where the seafood was from and took all the time in the world as he probably assumed they had more money than we did. Needless to say he got the tip that he earned for the service he gave us. I would absolutely go back for the food, just hope I would get a different server.

So as a Charlotte resident since 2006, I've known about the Cajun Queen since day one. Suffice to say, it's poor form on my part that the first time that I visited the famous cajun restaurant on 7th street was only a few weeks ago. 

On a Groupon.

After almost nine years.

Yeah, that might be me not getting out enough, but what that gap did for me (and why it's relevant to this review), was create an air of mysterious anticipation. Having heard fond stories from my peers and others who recommended it it time after time while I hadn't experienced it first hand built the  Cajun Queen up in my mind. This meant that with every passing day that my first visit would either be just that much greater of a manifestation of cajun superiority, or it would be that much further a fall from the lofty heights of expectations grown too large.

So my thoughts after my first visit?

Cajun Queen lives up to the hype. On a slightly less-than-comfortably-chilly night in Elizabeth, we were able to get a seat next to the fireplace, despite it being fairly busy. The building itself is an old turn-of-the-century home, and as such creates a very warm environment. We were downstairs, so we couldn't catch the live jazz band upstairs, but maybe next time. 

I ordered the bourbon-glazed pork chops, which, I know aren't terribly cajun, but damn I saw the guy next to me get them and I was sold. Everything came out quick enough, the pork chops were steaming hot with a beautiful sweet glaze that added a noticeable tang to the meat. Speaking of which, the pork was tender, the cuts were huge, and the taste was perfect. The meal went perfectly with an Abita beer, straight from New Orleans.

While we didn't get any appetizers or desserts, we were incredibly satisfied with the meal, the service and the fact that an establishment could live up to the considerable hype surrounding it. I recommend the Cajun Queen whether this is your first day in Charlotte, or you've been here for almost a decade!
Food was amazing. I had the Dianne and it was everything I imagined it would be. We had a seat next to the fireplace which set the mood perfect!

Cajun Queen is great for Charlotte but it's not the best cajun/creole I've had.  In my opinion, their food is good but leave's something to be desired if you've had great cajun/creole food. The apps here are good and the etouffee is alright.  Definitely make reservations when you come, as they only serve dinner (brunch on Sundays) and always have a crowd. They have "complimentary" valet service, and I would definitely recommend using it since they don't have an assigned lot. The live band is great and the service is very attentive. Solid restaurant if you want something different from the norm in the QC.
Absolutely delicious. The fried green tomato app was my favorite! The salad starter wasn't anything special, definitely get the gumbo. Can't wait to go back.

Visited today for Sunday brunch(party of 2)....Had a reservation, seated right away, were given our choice of seating area..We chose the back room(?) with all the fleur-de-lis pictures on the wall..There was a slight "odor" in the air, most likely from the mop water but soon forgot about it once the food came..Our server was Erin(correct spelling?) and he  was very good in explaining the Brunch menu,  etc..We didn't order adult beverages so I can't comment on the bar..We decided to go with the large order of the fried oysters and the barbecue shrimp and a bowl of of seafood gumbo... not  bad but nothing special...would not order in the future...But the fried oysters, WOW!! can definitely say they are some of if not the best we ever had!! Huge, perfect amount of breading, juicy and so tasty!! The barbecue shrimp were just about as good, sopped up every drop of broth with the complimentary bread(warm rolls) provided..And for dessert if you may,  Beignets  !! They looked great, and tasted just as great , still hot from the fryer with a perfect dusting of powered sugar and a strawberry compote(jam?) dipping sauce..Delicious!!  On the way out, we both used the restrooms(madame and monsieur) and both very clean ..And a big bonus, dined with a groupon..I definitely recommend the Cajun Queen and will be back, hopefully for dinner to catch the live jazz band playing there nightly..

Very dissatisfied and disappointed.  Will not go back.  Went over year ago and was disappointed in the shrimp and grits.  This time,  gave another shot and tried oysters and shrimp.  They were good but the only options to come with it was mashed potatoes and coleslaw and broccoli.   The very bland potatoes were cold, the slaw my husband got was not good, & the broccoli was just a giant tree on the plate.   The side house salad we ordered for an additional $4 was awful.   There were romaine core in the salad and one slice of cucumber.  The leaves were so huge that it looked like it was just thrown on the plate without thought.  The waiter was loud and annoying and our drinks ran out several times.   Having to ask someone to refill drinks.....the "complimentary" valet was not something I want forced on us either but we had no choice.  When it was time to retrieve our car, it was raining and we had to get it ourselves because the drivers were too busy parking other cars to get ours.  Do not go here if you want good food and a nice evening.

Cajun / Nola in the Charlotte, Yes please. 

This place has many traditional New Orleans options in a cool looking old house made into a restaurant. All kinds of meat, seafood, and good grub. 

I had the New Orleans B.B.Q. Shrimp (sautéed with butter, garlic, beer and a variety of Cajun/Creole spices. Served over rice). This dish was top notch and made me very happy.

Taking down one star because the service could have been better and more friendly.

They have live music upstairs but since I was here to catchup with old co-workers, we took the first floor so we could talk.

Will be back during a future CLT trip.

When I came to Charlotte in 2009, Cajun Queen was one of the first restaurants I visited.  The food was amazing!!!  When family and friends came to town I took them there. They all raved about the food.  The past three times have been very disappointing!  I went there yesterday for dinner. The service was good the food not so much.  I ordered the Etouffée with all three my sister ordered the Diane with chicken and shrimp.  We both were unhappy with our food and the basket of biscuits that were rock hard. I don't know if there is new management or they're cutting back on seasonings to cut cost.  Either way I will not go back. Sad, I really liked this place!!
Great service and food! The shrimp creole was really good. We really wanted beignets but those are only served on Sunday.

Love this place. I always order the blackened catfish with the shrimp topping in sauce. Stupendous!!! The Oreo cheesecake is mouth watering goodness!! I especially like sitting upstairs near the band after 6 pm!! My 4 year old needs entertainment at restaurants and he loves it!!

We went there on a Friday without a reservation. We were told that it could be an hour wait. But the hostess was very unfriendly, it was our first visit there and did not feel welcomed at all. We ended up no eating there. I don't care how good your food is if staff is unfriendly I  am not going in there. We drove back to our go to place Razzoo.

After an absence of 10 months we went to the Queen with an out town guest and another couple. Gumbo was good with a couple of shrimp and a staple of the place - good, not great but consistent. 3 of us had the fish special with crawfish topping and all liked but I gotta say my salmon was perfectly cooked - great job top chief. Our problem tonight was our server. He was just not that in to it. Sighs when asked to explain a dish, just crabby. He seemed to know what he was doing, just didn't want to be there.  Food rates a 5 star rating but service gets in the way. Too bad for all of us!

Try to eat here when schedule permits when in town for the race.  Had the blackened catfish for dinner as well as bbq shrimp appetizer and fried green tomatoes. Fish was plentiful and not overly spicy. Fried green tomatoes were the appetizer hit for the table.

Other dishes included salt and pepper catfish and bbq pork chop. Dessert included bread pudding and keylime pie.  Overall, another solid performance and prices are reasonable. Probably 4.5 stars.

The food was good. The service sucks!!! The staff is unfriendly and rude. I had a reservation for a big party and we were treated like unwanted guest. If the staff was on point including the valet parkers who were also rude then I would give it a 4 but honestly we will not be returning back!!!

Fantastic place with fantastic food, seriously loved the sevice, the ambiance and especially the dishes. Its a nice setting too.

I had the shrimp and the ettouffe, and I will seriously visit this place everytime i'm in Charlotte

We came in for brunch one weekend and the banana foster French toast was seriously to die for! Though the interior and decor left me expecting a bit more, the service was wonderful. I'm interested to try their dinner menu though

Well.i was highly disappointed, because I heard such good things.  I've spent years in new Orleans,and this place was far from being anything like it, in the food sense.I had the seafood gumbo, and it was like someone dumped the rosemary spice box in it. Terrible.. service was good except, just got the gumbo and the main course showed up 1 minute later. So of course, I refused it. So after 15 minutes under the heat lamp..you get the picture. .the etouffe was bland anyway. Trying cajun yard dog next. . If that's a bust, so much for cajun in charlotte.

I haven't been to a lot of Cajun Restaurants (yet), but this has hands down been my favorite. Pulling up it looks like a old historic house. I'd never eaten in a restaurant like this so I was excited to get inside. When you pull in, they have complimentary valet. They work really hard so I always make sure I have cash to tip them. One weekends you have to have a reservation as they are normally booked to capacity. Immediately at the door they have someone waiting to seat you. And inside, the layout is just like a house! I love it!! Tables are spacious and the atmosphere is very nice. I've eaten upstairs once and I will never do it again. The reason is because they have a band upstairs every night. While the music is nice, it is loud. I left with a headache that one time from trying to yell over the music along with all the other conversations going on as the bar is upstairs as well. Downstairs you can still hear the music so I prefer to eat there. I've never had a rude server. They are always so nice. I've tried a little bit of everything here, and the only thing that I can say left me something to be desired was the BBQ Shrimp. Not that flavorful, wasn't really exciting, I'll pass on that from now on. The popcorn Crawfish is soooo good! So tender! They just melt in your mouth. I wasn't a fan of the shrimp scampi. While it was delicious!! It was pretty much shrimp served in a soup of oil and butter. Was wayyy too much! And the seafood Gumbo is really good. It has a small kick of heat and you'll get a couple shrimp in it if you're lucky. My favorite meals are the All 3 Diane and the Special where you pick your fish and either Shrimp or Crawfish topping. Just about everything is served over rice but I prefer Mashed Potatoes. And the hands down best dessert there is the Bourbon Pecan Pie!!! OMG!!!!!! Just think 21 Jump Street in my mouth!! So delicious! We thought the bread pudding was pretty bland though. Not much going on flavor wise, which was disappointing because I was excited to try it. Overall this place is awesome! Highly recommend!

I ordered the Crawfish Étouffée, which I found disappointing. The roux was slightly burnt and very bland. My husband ordered the Gumbo and Diane. Diane he stated was ok, but the Gumbo was a disappointment. Based on first impressions, these dishes are not a due over.

We had 6:00 reservations on a Friday night. We arrived at 5:35 and were happy when our table was already available (holiday weekend so maybe not as crowded as a normal Friday night). We sat in the back which is a sunroom. We loved it and it seemed a little quieter than the rest of the restaurant. 

Bread- good but not spectacular. Side and Caesar salads- also decent but nothing special.  Great beer, wine, and mixed drink selection. They have a small kids menu and there were kids in the restaurant but it was more of an adult place in my mind. I don't think you can overdress because it's a nice (and pretty pricey) restaurant, but you can also come in with a nice pair of jeans. 

For appetizers our group split the BBQ shrimp and fried pickles. The shrimp was wonderful, spicy but bearable:) it was large, juicy, and cooked perfectly (not rubbery). The broth is amazing especially using it as a dip for the rolls. Fried pickles were typical fried pickles with ranch dip. Nothing unique, but still delicious.

Everyone loved their meals with the exception of one person in our party. First, the good. I ordered the special for $25- blackened tilapia over rice with a sauce of crawfish, sundried tomatoes, lemon, and artichoke. HEAVEN! Huge piece of fish (I brought 1/2 my meal home) and it melted in my mouth. The mixture of flavors was on point. 

Now, the bad. One man in our group is obsessed with steak and got the ribeye. The cut of meat was GIANT but it was pretty flavorless. It was cooked correctly but not what any of us would call worth $30. It came with a side of very dry, almost inedible, broccoli. But, it wasn't my meal (I just tried a bite!), so not knocking my review because of it. :)

Great place! I've never been to New Orleans, but my dad has and he is a huge fan of Cajun food, so I thought it would be nice to take him to brunch there. We were all really impressed. My mom and I had the Creole shrimp and grits and my dad had biscuits and gravy. We also got an order of beignets. The beignets are a definite must! 
The Cajun Queen is a great brunch place, we will definitely be back for dinner some time.

I just LOVE this place.  Best experience is sitting upstairs at the bar.  Order the NOLA BBQ Shrimp; Crawfish Etouffe; fish specials (seems like these never change, come to think of it....); blackened pork tenderloin with plantains and black bean mash.  PLUS live jazz every darn night.  What's not to love?

The flavors are so rich and the portions are awesome. Service was a little slow given there wasn't a big size. But the food made up for that. I would recommend this restaurant to everyone who enjoys fine dining. Also the ambiance makes it a great spot for a date night or anniversary. Throughly enjoyed my first experience. Can't wait to return.
Best Cajun that I have had outside New Orleans.  Service was fabulous,  Eat on the second floor for the smooth jazz.

Happy to have the complimentary valet. This restaurant used to be tough to visit because of that! The setting experience was worth it though.  We went once a while back, and returned recently for our anniversary.

The Diane is a must try dish, and if you can manage, go and eat upstairs when the band is playing. It really sets the tone and transports your whole evening.

Enjoyed the creole with chicken. Great spices snd flavors used in dish. Waiter was very knowledgeable and helped with picking the right entree especially it being first time eating Cajun food.  Ended our meal with the toll house cookie pie...YUM!

My husband and I flew into and out of Charlotte for a wedding about 4 weeks ago and were lucky enough to spot this place for lunch over the weekend. We shared Chicken Diane (Mushrooms, garlic, butter, green onions, parsley and our Queen's magic spices - all sautéed together. Moderately spiced and served over rice) and some Bignets for dessert (on the brunch menu). We loved the food we ordered so much- and one plate was definitely enough to share. The service was friendly and fast. If we are ever in the Charlotte area, we definitely plan to come back!

Ambiance, atmosphere, service, food... all exceeded expectations. The complimentary valet also add a nice touch. Making reservations on an early Friday evening should allow you to capture the experience at its best. ciao!

The food was very good. The service was fast and our server was very friendly. I really liked the live jazz band that was playing upstairs it helped with the authentic New Orleans feel. The complimentary valet was a nice touch. We will definitely come back to the Cajun Queen in the near future.

The fried oysters appetizer is super yummy as is the Diane with rice, shrimp and crawfish. Great atmosphere. Made reservations and were good to go as soon as we arrived, which has always been the case when I've made reservations here. Highly recommend it !

We took advantage of a $40 Groupon on a Tuesday night.  The evening was wonderful with good food, good wine, and good service (Thx Anna).  We were seated upstairs in a little corner and listened to the band while sipping an Old Vine Zinfandel--hard to top!

My wife took advantage of their 30 yr anniversary menu for $30; me, a 1 lbs. ribeye with Mushroom Diana on top.  There was so much food we split our entrees and doggy-bagged 8 oz of steak (yummy the next day, too).  The ribeye was cooked a perfect medium rare.  Cajun Queen is a great place with valet parking which is a no-brainer.  

PS:  Tried booking through Open Table that stated no openings.  When I called direct, no problem.  Great . . . table for two, please!

I want to love Cajun Queen, I really do. I try to give restaurants the benefit of the doubt when they fall short, understanding that things happen sometimes outside of their control. That said, Cajun Queen has continually failed to provide a satisfactory dining experience for us on 3 consecutive visits. The food alone would earn 4 stars for the advertised menu prices - although they do offer special discount deals fairly often. The customer service however is consistently dissapointing, to the point where I am convinced that the management staff needs to be changed. The attitude toward customers is not one of "How can I help make your experience better?" it instead seems to me that all of the workers are more into talking to eachother while dropping items at tables without saying a word. This is not just one bad egg, it seems to be everyone from the water boy to the manager. A friendly restaurant employee is the exception to the rule at Cajun Queen. In my opinion the lack of customer service ability is a direct result of the management failing to instill those abilities in their employees. 

If you get seated at the two person table in a hallway between the kitchen and 2 dining rooms just ask to be moved. That table is terrible and does not belong in any restaurant that has any respect for its customers. And that's just it, there seems to be a lack of respect amongst the staff for their customers here. The hostess at the door stares at her computer while talking to you without ever making eye contact, the bread boy just drops the bread at your table without a word. Water boy, same thing. Server doesn't exchange pleasantries, just straight to drinks and apps. Manager walks by and talks to his buddy about the game but doesn't acknowledge the guest at the table as his conversation is overpowering ours. Workers come barelling through with a table they are moving without saying 'pardon me' or anything at all. On the way out the door the manager guy just stands there staring at the hostess' computer screen without so much as saying thanks have a good night...

We have kept returning to Cajun Queen always hoping our next experience would prove to be better, but sadly I think we have now given up. The food earns a 4 star recomendation and it is worth experiencing, but the service is 2 star at best.
The only thing I get here is the pork tenderloin which I LOVE every time. Very consistent! Prices are expensive and service is not very friendly.  Environment is charming! Love the old house.

Good Cajun food is sometime hard to find, so bookmark this place.
If you are in the Charlotte, NC are make sure you plan a dinner stop at this establishment.

The best Cajun Cookin' I've had outside of Louisiana.

The Étouffée was delicious, I had it with Chicken, Shrimp, Crawfish, and Andouille Sausage, and its was perfect. All the protines were cooked perfectly. The spice and flavour was outstanding.

First time in Charlotte and went to Cajun Queen with my partner. The ambiance was great, our server was perfect and the food was amazing! I promise we will visit Cajun Queen for date night every time we visit Charlotte! :)

The service is very casual as is the entire restaurant. Service is great.

The food is ok, nothing special. The shrimp crab gumbo was pretty good but not hot (as in temp.) enough. The blackened catfish was a huge portion but disappointing, all paprika & chill powder no other seasoning! The veg served was thumbs down, room temp. Broccoli and flavorless over boiled mash potato's! One of the few times I left the starch on the plate.

The meal wasn't bad but acceptable at best!

Wonderful ambiance, fantastic food, and great service. I was in Charlotte and visited Cajun Queen for dinner. There was a small wait so our party headed up to the bar and decided to eat in the bar area. While the bar was busy the bartender was very attentive and delivered great service for both our food and bar orders. This being our first visit the bartender gave some recommendations that were fantastic. The bbq shrimp and fried green tomatoes appetizers were top notch. I had the Duck special that was wonderful and full of great flavor. The bourbon bread pudding was another great choice to finish out the meal. If you are looking for great cajun food in Charlotte this is the place.

We sat upstairs so we could hear the band, that was ok. What I loved was the atmosphere it reminded me of a spot in Brooklyn. The food was excellent I had the shrimp and grits, and the pumpkin cheesecake "LOVED IT".  We would definitely come back.
My wife and I always have a wonderful time at the Queen.  This time we took a friend of mine from Indy out for dinner and as usual the meal and sevice shined.

I was excited about eating tasty, authentic Cajun food.  Really confused about the reason our experience and food did not match up to the other reviews that I read before booking my reservation.

We came here to celebrate a successful event at work. We were a party of five very diverse diners but we all left food on our plates because it was average.  The men actually left seafood and meat in the portions they left on the table because the tastes were so bland.

Watery gumbo started off our meals. It was similar to the consistency of Progresso soups, we could have saved these calories and yes it has shrimp, sausage but why is gumbo so transparent and without a hint a peppers, garlic, etc. We pressed on.

Our party's entree choices were all different some had Diane,  Creole and a few combined appetizers to make an entree. No one finished their meal. Only one person even bothered to take home their leftovers.

The hostess was wonderful, the waiter was okay - he was not happy very curt with all his answers, he looked annoyed by our inquiries about menu items.  He should have just said if you don't know about our menu then you should not be here-boom!  The valet staff was pleasant, quick  and accommodating - Bravo!


We will go back because all the other reviews indicate that we had an unusual visit. I will update my review when I return.

So GOOD! My boss is from Charlotte and he told me I had to come here on my vacation. I did and I loved it! I ordered the Diane with everything and omg it was spectacular... 

The bartenders and waitresses were very friendly and resourceful although the hostess needs to check her attitude. either way, I didn't mind because I'm still daydreaming about that food! Nom city!

I've been to this restaurant many times! The food and service are great! I love the shrimp Diane! Previously parking was a nightmare, but they now offer complimentary valet! Definitely worth checking out!

I came  to charolette on 11/ 20 for my birthday weekend. My  friend made reservations for us to come to this restaurant. When you walk in, it looks like a house that was converted into a restaraunt which was awesome!  It definitely has a new orleans feel. We ordered drinks & appetizers. The  waiter also gave us a side of red beans and rice. I had a hurricane and fried green tomatoes. For my entrée,  I ordered fried catfish,  steamed broccoli and coleslaw and it was amazing!! The catfish filets were huge and plentiful! The  prices are very reasonable for the amount of food you get. The fish was seasoned and fried to perfection. The service, and ambience was amazing! My friend & I were celebrating our birthday,  the waiter gave us both a piece of pie of our choice on the house.  If your looking for a Cajun restaraunt, with a new orleans feel, please go to Cajun Queen you won't be disappointed!

Love NOLA? Then you'll love Cajun Queen. The atmosphere is beautifully inspired bu the best New Orleans has to offer. The food is AMAZING, seriously amazing. i had the gumbo and the New Orleans Platter and it was oh so tasty.

There were 10 of us here for a work dinner on a Wednesday night. The place wasn't too crowded but our table was right in front of the band upstairs and I was a little worried it was going to be crazy loud. Luckily it ended up being the best spot we could've gotten.

The table started with fried oysters and fried crawfish which you aren't going to go wrong with.  I ordered the ribeye and broccoli with a cup of gumbo. I wasn't crazy about the gumbo, and I thought it was a little thin and lacked any substance. Everyone else seemed to like it though. My ribeye was cooked and seasoned very well though with all that fried food in the beginning I couldn't finish it all. Two guys ordered some bread pudding for dessert and I tried some and it was awesome.

As for the music, they would play a few songs and then take a break so we could have conversations if we wanted. We had some Portuguese guys with us and someone asked them to play some Portuguese songs which apparently they did. You could tell the guy on the keyboards knew what he was doing and seemed to enter another world when he started playing. Overall it was a fun night with good food and everyone there seemed to enjoy themselves.
Very bad service. Spoiled the entire evening. I will definitely not visit this place ever again.

I was referred to Rankin by my general practitioner when I got that great big plus sign.  My OB here was Dr. Yavorski, who was sweet, encouraging and calm at all times - well, except for my last appointment when it seemed labor was imminent (it was) - then she was appropriately excited.  If you are going to Rankin for prenatal care and delivery, there is a team of 7 doctors (although I think one of them only practices at the Ballantyne location) and you will be encouraged to meet all of them as any one of them could be on call when you deliver.  I will say that I felt comfortable with all of the doctors.  They all exuded calmness, which was important to me.  Dr. Palermo actually ended up delivering me and her deadpan wit was the perfect thing to get me through the process.  I'd planned on an unmedicated birth, and the doctors were all supportive.  It wasn't until I went into labor and had a personal change of heart that I went for pain meds and they were supportive of that too.  I never felt like I was bullied or strong-armed into making a choice, and whenever I had questions they were answered to my satisfaction.  My pregnancy was pretty uneventful so I never really got to see them work in a crisis though. These doctors deliver at Presbyterian hospital, which is state of the art.
Well after everything I came out a healthy mom to a healthy baby boy, so I'm at least a fan.

Went today for the first time because of a referral by a friend. The facility is really nice and the personnel we're all extremely nice. Getting a "physical" is never a fun experience but doctor Yavorski was super quick and very gentle. She was very nice and asked thorough questions. I would highly recommend her to anyone looking for a new OBGYN!!
Dr Palermo delivered my son. I absolutely loved her and her care. She is in high demand so I don't get to see her during exams but will definitely have her delivery my future babies!

I have been a patient with Rankin's Women Center for just about 20 years and I hope Dr. Palermo never retires.  My review won't do justice to the enormous amount of gratitude I have for her, she is by far one of the most outstanding doctors I've ever had the pleasure of knowing.  Dr. Palermo listens to me.  She takes her time to have a discussion, to answer my questions, she gives me support when I need it, and she is outstanding at her profession.  I've lucky to have found such a compassionate and caring Dr. in a conveniently located office (although I did prefer the other office atmosphere better ;) )
Kudos to everyone at Rankin Women's Center for standing above the rest!

I'm constantly amazed by how rude the receptionists are. Not to mention my doctor, Dr. Palermo, left the practice and I never got a notification. If seeking an office that cares (even just a little bit), avoid this group.

I had been referred to Dr. Svendsen at Rankins Women's Center several years ago by a friend. I am so happy that I decided to switch to this practice and specifically to Dr. Svendsen. He is the only medical doctor that I have every been to who actually sits down and listens to your concerns and addresses each and every one before you leave.  Although there is often a wait time I'm confident it is because Dr. Svendsen is being as thorough as he can be with each and every patient which everyone deserves. To try to bypass the wait I try to make my appointments in the mornings when I can.  The receptionists and the nurses have always been very nice to me and very helpful and responsive when I have had questions about health insurance and coverage.  I am due March 2015 and very confident that I am receiving the best care possible. Now that my husband has met Dr. Svendsen he agrees that there are not many doctors out there that truly care like he does. I would recommend Dr. Svendsen to anyone looking for a new OBGYN.

The receptionist, Lillian  (or Vivian),  whatever her name was, she was VERY rude!  I'm not  planning on being a patient here if I don't feel welcome before I even step in the door. Fire Vivian (or Lillian)  whatever her name is,  and hire someone who doesn't have a problem doing their job. I have insurance, good insurance, so it's not like you guys aren't getting paid. - ANNOYED and VERY disappointed.

This is the branch where I got my mortgage for my first home 2 years ago. It was right before the dooky started flying around broke folks like me getting mortgages, so I don't know if they are handing out these puppies like the hotcakes they were back in good old 2006; however, I was really pleased with the service I got here. I had a lot of questions as a first time home buyer, and both of the guys who helped me out were patient with me and explained things in a way I could understand. They discouraged me from taking one of those evil ARMs, which would have gotten me a lot more house, but also would have lead to me eventually becoming one of those people on the news.
